# BMW Product Idea Evaluation

Feature decisions for the BMW 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60) and 7 Series (G70), traced to the data in `BMW-Data/`: 10,128 customer comments, the 2025 customer studies (CN/EU and US), sales volumes 2024–2030 and the German price lists (July 2026).

A product manager types a feature idea ("make seat massage standard on the 5 Series in Europe"). Three agents and a deterministic decision engine answer it:

1. **Retriever agent** (`gpt-6-luna`) matches the idea to features in a **knowledge graph** of all processed data and model outputs, reads the scope (series, markets, move, price) and returns a validated Pydantic `IdeaSpec`. The PM confirms or edits it.
2. **Decision engine** (no LLM) computes every number: per series and market **Prioritise / Consider / Low priority / Insufficient evidence / Not sold** from complaints, breadth, requests, survey weakness and sales volume, plus the price-list position. It emits a bundle of facts, each with a stable ID and a pointer into the graph (table row, PDF page or model file).
3. **Explainer agent** (`gpt-6-terra`) writes a brief for product management in which every claim cites fact IDs.
4. **Verifier agent** (rules + `gpt-6-luna`) checks each claim: citations exist, every number matches a cited value, labels and quotes match, the series and markets named are covered, and the cited facts entail the claim. Failing claims go back for one rewrite and are removed if they still fail.

Weights and market emphasis are an explicit, hashed policy. Two PMs using the same policy and data get the same answer, and a PM override is logged with its rationale.

```
python -m bmw_feedback serve          # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

The full analysis is in **[reports/REPORT.md](reports/REPORT.md)**.

---

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
# put the hackathon files in BMW-Data/ (git-ignored)

python -m bmw_feedback all            # build + train + knowledge graph + figures (~6 min)
cd frontend && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
python -m bmw_feedback serve          # API + web app on http://127.0.0.1:8000

python -m pytest tests -q             # graph, agents (scripted LLM, no network) and API checks
```

### OpenAI key and models

The explainer and verifier need an OpenAI key; without one the app still matches ideas (with transparent rules and TF-IDF) and shows all evidence, and says that the written brief is unavailable. Put the key in the environment or in a git-ignored `.env` in the repository root:

```
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
OPENAI_RETRIEVER_MODEL=gpt-6-luna         # defaults shown; override any of them
OPENAI_EXPLAINER_MODEL=gpt-6-terra
OPENAI_VERIFIER_MODEL=gpt-6-luna
REDACTED
```

`python -m bmw_feedback agent --check` lists which configured models the key can use. A model the key cannot use is reported with the available ones; it is never swapped silently. `python -m bmw_feedback agent "your idea"` runs the whole pipeline in the terminal.

### BMW logo and font (local only)

The official BMW logo and BMW Type Next are BMW's trademark and licensed font. They are not in the repository. `frontend/scripts/fetch-brand-assets.cjs` fetches them from bmw.de into the git-ignored `frontend/public/brand` and `frontend/public/fonts` for local use (it needs Playwright). Without them the app shows a text wordmark and uses Barlow.

For frontend development, run `npm run dev` in `frontend/` (port 5173). It proxies `/api` to the server on port 8000.

Command-line access works without the app:

```bash
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --feature "head-up display"
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --text "The wireless charger keeps overheating my phone"
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --list
```

## The web app

One page, built for evaluating an idea:

| Section | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Idea | Free-text input, then the retriever's reading of it: candidate features (with how each was found: name/alias, classifier, semantic), series, markets, move and price, all editable before evaluation |
| Pipeline | The four steps (retriever, decision engine, explainer, verifier) with the model behind each and its result |
| Overview | Key figures: priority score, Prioritise / Consider cells, evidence coverage, customer verdict, claims verified |
| Explanation | The brief for product management; every claim has numbered citations that open the fact and its source and can jump to the node in the graph |
| Series × markets | Recommendation matrix with an evidence panel per cell (signals, weights, reasons, quotes, survey rows, price-list items) |
| Price & equipment | Price ladder across the three series and the linked technical data |
| Knowledge graph | The part of the graph this evaluation touched (cited nodes ringed) and a schema view of how all the data connects; a node inspector shows each node's source, attributes and relations |
| Verification | Every claim with the result of each rule and the entailment check; what was rewritten and what was removed |
| Decision | Adjustable decision policy and the decision record (accept / override with rationale, logged with policy and data hashes) |

Design: tokens measured on bmw.de (`--cta #1c69d4`, `--nba #262626`, `--border #e6e6e6`, status pairs, 3px controls, 84px navigation, 300/500/700 weights, uppercase stage headline, sticky in-page tab bar, technical-data fact rows). Content cards use 12–16px corners by product choice. See `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css`.

## Knowledge graph and agents

`python -m bmw_feedback graph` writes `data/processed/knowledge_graph.json` (networkx, node-link; about 15,000 nodes and 58,000 edges) and `graph_schema.json`. The build checks node and edge counts against the source tables (224 features, 10,128 comments, 11,214 feature labels, 23 variants, 364 price-list items, 2,224 option fitment rows, 1,494 feature fitment rows, 1,442 survey answer shares, …) and fails on any mismatch. Dashboard re-exports, figure statistics and model internals are left out on purpose; the list is in `graph_schema.json`.

| Node types | From |
|---|---|
| Series, Variant, Powertrain, OptionItem, Package, FitmentSummary, TechSpec | price-list PDFs (page references) |
| Market, SalesVolume, FeedbackCoverage | sales_volumes.xlsx, market representativeness |
| Domain, Feature, Reason, ReasonFamily, Comment | feedback exports, taxonomy |
| SurveyAttribute, SurveyScore | customer studies |
| VerdictCell, ModelArtifact, EBMTerm | scoring, classifiers, complaint EBM, fitment re-ranker |
| Caveat | limits of the data, computed from it (e.g. "the G70 equipment tables cover 4 of 7 variants") |

```
bmw_feedback/graph/    build.py (graph + validation), store.py (load, node inspector), semantic.py (feature index)
bmw_feedback/agents/   contracts.py (Pydantic), retriever.py, facts.py, explainer.py, verifier.py, evidence.py, pipeline.py, llm.py
```

API: `POST /api/agent/interpret`, `POST /api/agent/evaluate`, `POST /api/agent/explain`, `GET /api/agent/status`, `GET /api/graph/schema`, `GET /api/graph/node/{id}`.

## Pipeline

```
BMW-Data/*.xlsx, *.PDF
   │  load.py            feedback, CN/EU + US surveys, sales volumes
   │  option_catalog.py  price-list PDFs: variants, base prices, ■/□ fitment per variant, option prices,
   │                     packages, technical data; validated on every build
   ▼
clean.py                 one row per comment + one row per label; strip label leakage and templates
taxonomy.py              11 domains ← 224 features ← 84 reasons; survey and price-list link maps
scoring.py               channel-adjusted complaint / praise / request indices with 95% intervals → verdict
classifier.py            TF-IDF + logistic regression: comment → type, domain, feature
                         (+ price-list fitment re-ranker when the car is known)
risk_model.py            explainable boosting machine: what drives complaints (glass box)
decision.py              idea → features → per series × market recommendation + suggested move
graph/                   knowledge graph of the processed tables and model outputs (validated against the sources;
                         the few deliberate exclusions are listed in graph_schema.json)
agents/                  retriever → decision engine facts → explainer → verifier
api.py                   FastAPI; serves frontend/dist
```

### What the price lists feed

The PDFs are parsed from glyph and text positions, not from text order. Every build checks that:
- all 1,889 ■/□ marks on the 32 table pages land in a variant column;
- all 1,128 option prices and 23 base prices satisfy gross = net × 1.19;
- power on the price pages matches the technical data for all 23 variants.

One printed anomaly (F70 p.17) is kept as printed. 106 feedback features are linked to price-list items through a curated keyword map, and each link shows the keyword that produced it.

| Layer | Use of the price lists | Measured effect |
|---|---|---|
| Feature classifier | Re-ranks candidates by the feature's fitment on the comment's car | +0.6 pp top-1 on comments about linked features (26 fixed, 4 broken, McNemar p = 0.0001) |
| Complaint model | Fitment tier, option price and % of base price as inputs | No held-out gain (AUC −0.0008, feature-grouped CV), so the production model uses context only; the price-list variant is kept for audit |
| Decision engine | Price ladder across series, standard vs optional vs not listed, suggested move | Deterministic, with page references |

## Outputs

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reports/REPORT.md` | Findings, method, roadmap |
| `reports/model_ablation.json` | Price-list ablations for both models, EBM shape functions |
| `reports/classifier_metrics.json`, `data_quality.json` | Classifier CV metrics, cleaning and PDF-validation counts |
| `data/processed/catalog_*.csv` | Parsed price lists: variants, items, fitment, packages, technical data, feature links |
| `data/processed/knowledge_graph.json`, `graph_schema.json` | Knowledge graph and its schema with the integrity checks |
| `data/decisions.jsonl` | Decision log written by the app (git-ignored) |

## Repository layout

```
bmw_feedback/     pipeline package, knowledge graph, agents and API
frontend/         React + Vite web app (built into frontend/dist)
tests/            graph, agent and API checks
docs/             design spec
reports/          report, figures, scorecards, metrics
BMW-Data/         raw hackathon data (not committed)
```

This repository previously held **Demandra**, our procurement demand-prediction solution for Challenge 2 of the Unite x TUM.ai Hackathon (1st place). The original code is in git history.

"""OpenAI access for the three agents.

Configuration (environment variables, or a git-ignored `.env` file in the repo root):
    OPENAI_API_KEY             required for the LLM agents and embeddings
    OPENAI_RETRIEVER_MODEL     default gpt-6-luna   (Agent 1: idea -> IdeaSpec)
    OPENAI_EXPLAINER_MODEL     default gpt-6-terra  (Agent 2: facts -> PM explanation)
    OPENAI_VERIFIER_MODEL      default gpt-6-luna   (Agent 3: semantic check of each claim)
    OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL     default text-embedding-3-small (semantic matching of ideas)

A configured model that the account cannot use is reported with the models it can
use; it is never replaced by another model silently.
"""

import os
import threading

import numpy as np
from pydantic import BaseModel

from .. import config

ROLES = ("retriever", "explainer", "verifier", "embedding")
DEFAULT_MODELS = {"retriever": "gpt-6-luna", "explainer": "gpt-6-terra", "verifier": "gpt-6-luna",
                  "embedding": "text-embedding-3-small"}
ENV_VARS = {"retriever": "OPENAI_RETRIEVER_MODEL", "explainer": "OPENAI_EXPLAINER_MODEL",
            "verifier": "OPENAI_VERIFIER_MODEL", "embedding": "OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL"}


class LLMError(RuntimeError):
    """A call to the language model failed or returned nothing usable."""


class LLMUnavailable(LLMError):
    """No API key is configured."""


class ModelUnavailable(LLMError):
    """The configured model is not available to this API key."""


class LLMOutputInvalid(LLMError):
    """The model's structured output did not validate against the requested schema."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, errors: list[str]):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.errors = errors


def _dotenv() -> dict:
    path = config.ROOT / ".env"
    out = {}
    if path.exists():
        for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
                continue
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            out[k.strip().removeprefix("export ").strip()] = v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return out


def setting(name: str, default: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    return os.environ.get(name) or _dotenv().get(name) or default


def model_config() -> dict:
    return {role: setting(ENV_VARS[role], DEFAULT_MODELS[role]) for role in ROLES}


class OpenAILLM:
    """Thin wrapper: structured parsing into Pydantic models, embeddings, model availability."""

    provider = "openai"

    def __init__(self, api_key: str, models: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 180.0):
        from openai import OpenAI
        self.client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key, timeout=timeout, max_retries=2)
        self.models = models or model_config()
        self._available: set | None = None
        self._listing_error: str | None = None
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- availability
    def available_models(self, refresh: bool = False) -> set | None:
        """Model ids this key can use, or None if the key may not list models."""
        import openai
        with self._lock:
            if self._available is None or refresh:
                try:
                    self._available = {m.id for m in self.client.models.list()}
                    self._listing_error = None
                except openai.AuthenticationError as e:
                    raise LLMError(f"OpenAI rejected the API key: {_msg(e)}") from e
                except openai.OpenAIError as e:
                    self._available, self._listing_error = None, _msg(e)
            return self._available

    def check_models(self, refresh: bool = False) -> dict:
        avail = self.available_models(refresh)
        roles = {r: {"model": m, "available": None if avail is None else m in avail} for r, m in self.models.items()}
        similar = sorted(m for m in (avail or ()) if m.startswith(("gpt-6", "gpt-5", "text-embedding")))
        return {"roles": roles, "listing_error": self._listing_error, "similar_models": similar[:40]}

    def _model(self, role: str) -> str:
        model = self.models[role]
        avail = self.available_models()
        if avail is not None and model not in avail:
            options = sorted(m for m in avail if m.startswith(("gpt-", "text-embedding")))
            raise ModelUnavailable(f"The {role} model '{model}' is not available to this API key. Set "
                                   f"{ENV_VARS[role]} to one of: {', '.join(options[:30]) or '(none listed)'}")
        return model

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- calls
    def parse(self, role: str, instructions: str, input_text: str, schema: type[BaseModel]) -> BaseModel:
        import openai
        from pydantic import ValidationError
        model = self._model(role)
        try:
            resp = self.client.responses.parse(model=model, instructions=instructions, input=input_text,
                                               text_format=schema, store=False)
        except ValidationError as e:
            errors = [f"{'.'.join(str(x) for x in err['loc']) or 'output'}: {err['msg']}" for err in e.errors()]
            raise LLMOutputInvalid(f"{model} returned output that does not match {schema.__name__}", errors) from e
        except openai.OpenAIError as e:
            raise LLMError(f"{model}: {_msg(e)}") from e
        parsed = resp.output_parsed
        if parsed is None:
            raise LLMError(f"{model} returned no structured output (status {resp.status}, "
                           f"details {resp.incomplete_details})")
        return parsed

    def embed(self, texts: list[str], model: str | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
        import openai
        model = model or self._model("embedding")
        try:
            resp = self.client.embeddings.create(model=model, input=texts)
        except openai.OpenAIError as e:
            raise LLMError(f"{model}: {_msg(e)}") from e
        return np.array([d.embedding for d in resp.data], dtype=float)


def _msg(e: Exception) -> str:
    body = getattr(e, "body", None)
    if isinstance(body, dict) and isinstance(body.get("error"), dict):
        return body["error"].get("message") or str(e)
    return str(e)


def from_env() -> OpenAILLM | None:
    key = setting("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    return OpenAILLM(key) if key else None
"""Orchestrates the three agents around the decision engine.

    interpret(idea)            Agent 1 -> IdeaSpec + candidates             (PM confirms / edits)
    evaluate(spec, policy)     DecisionEngine -> FactBundle + evidence subgraph   (no LLM, instant)
    explain(evaluation_id)     Agent 2 writes -> Agent 3 verifies -> one rewrite -> strip what still fails
"""

import threading
import time
from collections import OrderedDict

from .. import config
from ..decision import MARKETS, merge_policy, policy_hash
from ..graph.semantic import SemanticIndex
from ..graph.store import get_graph
from . import explainer, verifier
from .contracts import SECTIONS, Explanation, IdeaSpec, VerificationReport
from .evidence import subgraph
from .facts import build_bundle, evaluation_id
from .llm import LLMUnavailable, from_env, model_config
from .retriever import Retriever

MAX_CACHED = 64


class UnknownEvaluation(LookupError):
    """The evaluation id is not (or no longer) in the cache."""

NO_KEY = ("No OpenAI API key is configured, so the explanation and verification agents cannot run. Set "
          "OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment or in a .env file in the repository root, then try again. The "
          "evidence above comes from the decision engine and does not need the key.")


class Pipeline:
    def __init__(self, engine, llm="env"):
        self.engine = engine
        self.g, self.graph_meta = get_graph()
        self.index = SemanticIndex(self.g)
        self.retriever = Retriever(engine, self.g, self.index)
        self._env_llm = llm == "env"
        self.llm = from_env() if self._env_llm else llm
        self.feature_names = set(engine.ctx.features.index)
        self._evals: OrderedDict = OrderedDict()
        self._candidates: OrderedDict = OrderedDict()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def _current_llm(self):
        """Pick up a key added to the environment or .env after start-up."""
        if self.llm is None and self._env_llm:
            self.llm = from_env()
        return self.llm

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ status
    def status(self, check: bool = False) -> dict:
        llm = self._current_llm()
        out = {"llm_configured": llm is not None, "provider": "openai",
               "models": llm.models if llm else model_config(),
               "graph": {"nodes": self.graph_meta["n_nodes"], "edges": self.graph_meta["n_edges"],
                         "built_at": self.graph_meta["built_at"],
                         "checks_passed": all(c["ok"] for c in self.graph_meta["checks"]),
                         "n_checks": len(self.graph_meta["checks"])},
               "message": None if llm else NO_KEY}
        if llm is not None and check:
            out["availability"] = llm.check_models(refresh=True)
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Agent 1
    def interpret(self, idea: str) -> dict:
        res = self.retriever.interpret(idea, self._current_llm())
        with self._lock:
            self._candidates[res.spec.idea] = res.candidates
            while len(self._candidates) > MAX_CACHED:
                self._candidates.popitem(last=False)
        return res.model_dump()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ engine + facts
    def evaluate(self, spec_data: dict, policy: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        spec = IdeaSpec.model_validate(spec_data, context={"allowed_features": self.feature_names})
        models = list(spec.series) or None
        markets = list(spec.markets) or None
        if spec.features:
            result = self.engine.evaluate("", [f.feature for f in spec.features], policy, models, markets)
            result["idea"] = spec.idea
        else:
            pol = merge_policy(policy)
            result = {"idea": spec.idea, "resolution": None, "features": [], "status": "no_direct_evidence",
                      "policy": pol, "policy_hash": policy_hash(pol), "data_hash": self.engine.fingerprint["hash"],
                      "models": models or list(config.MODELS), "markets": markets or list(MARKETS)}
        with self._lock:
            candidates = self._candidates.get(spec.idea)
        if candidates is None:
            candidates = self.retriever.candidates(spec.idea, self._current_llm())[0]
        eid = evaluation_id(spec, result["policy_hash"], result["data_hash"])
        bundle = build_bundle(self.engine, self.g, spec, result, candidates, eid)
        graph = subgraph(self.g, spec, result, bundle, candidates)
        with self._lock:
            prev = self._evals.get(eid)
            self._evals[eid] = {"spec": spec, "result": result, "bundle": bundle,
                                "explained": prev["explained"] if prev else None}
            self._evals.move_to_end(eid)
            while len(self._evals) > MAX_CACHED:
                self._evals.popitem(last=False)
        return {"evaluation_id": eid, "spec": spec.model_dump(), "result": result,
                "facts": [f.model_dump() for f in bundle.facts], "graph": graph,
                "candidates": [c.model_dump() for c in candidates]}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Agents 2 + 3
    def explain(self, eid: str, force: bool = False) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            entry = self._evals.get(eid)
        if entry is None:
            raise UnknownEvaluation(eid)
        if entry["explained"] and not force:
            return entry["explained"]
        llm = self._current_llm()
        if llm is None:
            raise LLMUnavailable(NO_KEY)
        t0 = time.time()
        spec, bundle = entry["spec"], entry["bundle"]
        claims = verifier.verify(explainer.to_claims(explainer.write(llm, bundle, spec), 1), bundle, llm)
        rewritten, attempts = [], 1
        if any(c.status == "removed" for c in claims):
            rewritten = [c for c in claims if c.status == "removed"]
            draft = explainer.write(llm, bundle, spec, feedback=rewritten)
            claims = verifier.verify(explainer.to_claims(draft, 2), bundle, llm)
            attempts = 2
        sections = {s: [c for c in claims if c.section == s and c.status == "verified"] for s in SECTIONS}
        explanation = Explanation(evaluation_id=eid, model=llm.models["explainer"], sections=sections,
                                  attempts=attempts)
        report = VerificationReport(evaluation_id=eid, rules=verifier.RULES, semantic_model=llm.models["verifier"],
                                    claims=claims, rewritten=rewritten,
                                    n_verified=sum(c.status == "verified" for c in claims),
                                    n_removed=sum(c.status == "removed" for c in claims))
        out = {"explanation": explanation.model_dump(), "verification": report.model_dump(),
               "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)}
        entry["explained"] = out
        return out
"""Pydantic contracts between the three agents, the decision engine and the frontend.

Models ending in `LLM` are what a language model is asked to return. They are
kept free of defaults and dict fields so OpenAI's strict structured outputs
accept them. Everything an LLM returns is then re-validated into the strict
models below with the context it must respect (e.g. the allowed feature names).
"""

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationInfo, field_validator, model_validator

Series = Literal["F70", "G60", "G70"]
Market = Literal["EU", "US", "CN", "RoW"]
Move = Literal["fix_existing", "make_standard", "new_option", "price_change", "introduce_on_series", "unspecified"]
Novelty = Literal["matches_existing", "related_only", "new_to_data"]
SERIES: tuple = ("F70", "G60", "G70")
MARKETS: tuple = ("EU", "US", "CN", "RoW")
MAX_FEATURES = 3

MOVE_LABELS = {
    "fix_existing": "Fix or improve what exists",
    "make_standard": "Make it standard equipment",
    "new_option": "Offer it as a new option",
    "price_change": "Change the price",
    "introduce_on_series": "Introduce it on another series",
    "unspecified": "Not specified",
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Agent 1: retriever
class Candidate(BaseModel):
    """A feature the code (not the LLM) found for the idea, with how it was found."""
    feature: str
    node_id: str
    domain: str
    verdict: str
    n_comments: int
    umbrella: bool
    methods: dict[str, float]          # e.g. {"alias": 1.0, "classifier": 0.42, "semantic": 0.61}
    how: list[str]                     # human-readable match reasons


class FeaturePickLLM(BaseModel):
    feature: str
    reason: str


class IdeaSpecLLM(BaseModel):
    summary: str
    features: list[FeaturePickLLM]
    series: list[Series]
    markets: list[Market]
    move: Move
    proposed_price_eur: float | None
    novelty: Novelty
    ambiguities: list[str]


class FeaturePick(BaseModel):
    feature: str
    node_id: str
    reason: str
    methods: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict)


class IdeaSpec(BaseModel):
    """What the idea is about, validated against the knowledge graph. Confirmed or edited by the PM."""
    idea: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    summary: str
    features: list[FeaturePick] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=MAX_FEATURES)
    series: list[Series] = Field(default_factory=list)       # empty = all series
    markets: list[Market] = Field(default_factory=list)      # empty = all markets
    move: Move = "unspecified"
    proposed_price_eur: float | None = None
    novelty: Novelty = "matches_existing"
    ambiguities: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    method: str = "rules"

    @field_validator("proposed_price_eur")
    @classmethod
    def _price_positive(cls, v):
        if v is not None and not (0 < v < 1_000_000):
            raise ValueError("proposed_price_eur must be a positive amount in EUR below 1,000,000")
        return v

    @field_validator("series", "markets")
    @classmethod
    def _unique(cls, v):
        if len(set(v)) != len(v):
            raise ValueError("duplicate entries")
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _graph_consistency(self, info: ValidationInfo):
        allowed = (info.context or {}).get("allowed_features")
        names = [f.feature for f in self.features]
        if len(set(names)) != len(names):
            raise ValueError("a feature is listed twice")
        if allowed is not None:
            unknown = [n for n in names if n not in allowed]
            if unknown:
                raise ValueError(f"features not among the retrieved candidates: {unknown}. "
                                 f"Choose only from: {sorted(allowed)}")
        for f in self.features:
            if f.node_id != f"feature:{f.feature}":
                raise ValueError(f"node_id {f.node_id!r} does not belong to feature {f.feature!r}")
        if self.novelty == "matches_existing" and not self.features:
            raise ValueError("novelty is 'matches_existing' but no feature was chosen")
        if self.novelty == "new_to_data" and self.features:
            raise ValueError("novelty is 'new_to_data' but features were chosen; use 'matches_existing' "
                             "or 'related_only'")
        return self


class InterpretResult(BaseModel):
    spec: IdeaSpec
    candidates: list[Candidate]
    semantic_method: str
    semantic_error: str | None = None
    method: str
    attempts: list[dict]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- facts (deterministic)
class Provenance(BaseModel):
    node_id: str | None                # knowledge-graph node (or request-time node such as rec:...)
    kind: str                          # table | pdf | xlsx | model | derived | config | engine | pm
    ref: str
    key: str | None = None
    page: int | None = None


class Fact(BaseModel):
    id: str
    group: str
    statement: str
    value: float | int | str | bool | None = None
    unit: str | None = None
    feature: str | None = None
    series: str | None = None
    market: str | None = None
    source: Provenance


class FactBundle(BaseModel):
    evaluation_id: str
    idea: str
    facts: list[Fact]

    def index(self) -> dict:
        return {f.id: f for f in self.facts}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Agent 2: explainer
SECTIONS = ["headline", "customer_evidence", "market_view", "price_and_equipment", "risks_and_caveats", "next_steps"]
SECTION_TITLES = {
    "headline": "Bottom line", "customer_evidence": "What customers say", "market_view": "Where it matters",
    "price_and_equipment": "Price and equipment today", "risks_and_caveats": "Risks and limits of the evidence",
    "next_steps": "Recommended next steps",
}


class ClaimLLM(BaseModel):
    text: str
    fact_ids: list[str]


class ExplanationLLM(BaseModel):
    headline: ClaimLLM
    customer_evidence: list[ClaimLLM]
    market_view: list[ClaimLLM]
    price_and_equipment: list[ClaimLLM]
    risks_and_caveats: list[ClaimLLM]
    next_steps: list[ClaimLLM]

    def claims(self) -> list[ClaimLLM]:
        return [self.headline] + [c for s in SECTIONS[1:] for c in getattr(self, s)]


class Check(BaseModel):
    name: str
    passed: bool
    detail: str


class Claim(BaseModel):
    id: str
    section: str
    text: str
    fact_ids: list[str]
    status: Literal["verified", "removed"] = "verified"
    attempt: int = 1
    checks: list[Check] = Field(default_factory=list)


class Explanation(BaseModel):
    evaluation_id: str
    model: str
    sections: dict[str, list[Claim]]       # section -> verified claims only
    attempts: int


class VerificationReport(BaseModel):
    evaluation_id: str
    rules: list[str]
    semantic_model: str | None
    claims: list[Claim]                    # final claims, verified and removed
    rewritten: list[Claim]                 # claims of the first draft that failed and triggered the rewrite
    n_verified: int
    n_removed: int


class JudgmentLLM(BaseModel):
    claim_id: str
    verdict: Literal["supported", "unsupported"]
    reason: str


class JudgmentsLLM(BaseModel):
    judgments: list[JudgmentLLM]

1	"""Feature-idea decision engine: one PM question in, a traceable per-market answer out.
2	
3	    idea text -> matched VFC features (alias / name / text classifier, PM confirms)
4	              -> per (model, market) cell: four evidence signals in [0, 1]
5	              -> weighted score -> Prioritise / Consider / Low priority
6	              -> action type from the DE price list (fix, make standard, introduce)
7	
8	Signals (each cites its source rows; a missing signal is shown, never imputed)
9	    complaints  channel-adjusted complaint verdict of the feature in that model + market
10	    breadth     how many of the model's customers raise the feature at all (percentile)
11	    requests    channel-adjusted request index ('Wants') in that model + market
12	    survey      how weak the matching survey attribute is in that model + market (percentile)
13	
14	Weights, market multipliers and thresholds are policy, not data: they live in
15	DEFAULT_POLICY, are returned with every result and hashed, so two PMs with the
16	same policy and data get the same answer and an override is visible.
17	"""
18	
19	import copy
20	import hashlib

64	def _hash(obj) -> str:
65	    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]

68	def data_fingerprint() -> dict:
69	    """Content hash of every raw input file, so a decision can be tied to the exact data."""
70	    files = sorted(config.RAW_DIR.glob("*"))
71	    h = hashlib.sha256()
72	    listing = []
73	    for f in files:
74	        if f.is_file():
75	            digest = hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
76	            h.update(f.name.encode() + digest.encode())
77	            listing.append({"file": f.name, "sha256": digest[:12], "bytes": f.stat().st_size})
78	    return {"hash": h.hexdigest()[:12], "files": listing}

83	    return _hash({k: policy[k] for k in ("version", "weights", "market_multipliers", "thresholds", "volume_year",

87	def merge_policy(overrides: dict | None) -> dict:
88	    policy = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_POLICY)
89	    for key in ("weights", "market_multipliers", "thresholds"):
90	        for k, v in ((overrides or {}).get(key) or {}).items():
91	            if k in policy[key] and v is not None:
92	                policy[key][k] = float(v)
93	    b = (overrides or {}).get("borrowing") or {}
94	    if "enabled" in b:
95	        policy["borrowing"]["enabled"] = bool(b["enabled"])
96	    if "into_cn" in b:
97	        policy["borrowing"]["into_cn"] = bool(b["into_cn"])
98	    if b.get("discount") is not None:
99	        policy["borrowing"]["discount"] = min(max(float(b["discount"]), 0.0), 1.0)
100	    if (overrides or {}).get("volume_year") in (2024, 2025, 2030):
101	        policy["volume_year"] = int(overrides["volume_year"])
102	    return policy

120	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ evidence tables
121	    def _breadth_table(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
122	        """Per model: comments mentioning each feature, and its percentile among the model's features."""
123	        u = self.units.drop_duplicates(["comment_id", "feature"])
124	        counts = u.groupby(["model", "feature"])["comment_id"].nunique().rename("n").reset_index()
125	        totals = self.ctx.labels.drop_duplicates("comment_id").groupby("model")["comment_id"].nunique()
126	        counts["model_comments"] = counts["model"].map(totals)
127	        counts["share"] = counts["n"] / counts["model_comments"]
128	        counts["percentile"] = counts.groupby("model")["n"].rank(pct=True, method="max")
129	        counts["n_features"] = counts.groupby("model")["feature"].transform("size")
130	        return counts.set_index(["model", "feature"])

132	    def _survey_ranks(self) -> dict:
133	        """(market, survey_model) -> attribute table with rank 1 = best-rated attribute."""
134	        out = {}
135	        s = self.survey_eu_cn[self.survey_eu_cn["attribute"] != "Overall product satisfaction"]
136	        for (market, model), g in s.groupby(["market", "model"]):
137	            g = g.assign(rank=g["mean"].rank(ascending=False, method="min"), n=len(g),
138	                         overall_mean=g["mean"].mean())
139	            out[(market, model)] = g.set_index("attribute")
140	        for model, g in self.survey_us.groupby("model"):
141	            g = g.assign(rank=g["top2_box"].rank(ascending=False, method="min"), n=len(g),
142	                         overall_top2=g["top2_box"].mean())
143	            out[("US", model)] = g.set_index("attribute")
144	        return out

146	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ idea -> features
147	    def resolve_idea(self, idea: str, top_k: int = 6) -> dict:
148	        from .classifier import predict
149	        matches = {}
150	        for m in self._name_matches(idea):
151	            matches[m["feature"]] = m
152	        pred = predict([idea])[0]
153	        for f, p in predict([idea], top_k=top_k)[0]["feature"]:
154	            if f not in matches and f in self.ctx.features.index:
155	                matches[f] = {"feature": f, "score": float(p), "how": "text classifier"}
156	        ranked = sorted(matches.values(), key=lambda m: -m["score"])
157	        for m in ranked:
158	            row = self.ctx.features.loc[m["feature"]]
159	            m.update(domain=row["domain"], n_comments=int(row["n_comments"]), verdict=row["verdict"],
160	                     umbrella=bool(row["is_umbrella"]))
161	        top = ranked[0]["score"] if ranked else 0
162	        status = "direct" if top >= 0.5 else "related" if top >= 0.15 else "none"
163	        return {"idea": idea, "status": status, "matches": ranked,
164	                "suggested": [m["feature"] for m in ranked if m["score"] >= 0.5][:2],
165	                "predicted_domains": [{"domain": d, "score": float(s)} for d, s in pred["domain"]],
166	                "predicted_feedback_type": [{"type": t, "score": float(s)} for t, s in pred["feedback_type"]]}

168	    def _name_matches(self, idea: str) -> list:
169	        """Alias, exact and substring matches score 1.0; fuzzy name matches score their similarity."""
170	        import difflib
171	        q = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", idea.strip().lower())
172	        if not q:
173	            return []
174	        names = list(self.ctx.features.index)
175	        aliases = _aliases()
176	        out = []
177	        if q in aliases:
178	            out.append({"feature": aliases[q], "score": 1.0, "how": "alias"})
179	        for n in names:
180	            nl = n.lower()
181	            if nl == q or (len(q) >= 4 and q in nl):
182	                out.append({"feature": n, "score": 1.0, "how": "feature name"})
183	        for alias, target in aliases.items():
184	            if len(alias) >= 4 and re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(alias)}\b", q) and q not in aliases:
185	                out.append({"feature": target, "score": 0.9, "how": f"alias '{alias}' in idea"})
186	        if not out:
187	            for n in names:
188	                ratio = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, q, n.lower()).ratio()
189	                if ratio >= 0.8:
190	                    out.append({"feature": n, "score": round(ratio, 2), "how": "fuzzy name"})
191	        seen, unique = set(), []
192	        for m in sorted(out, key=lambda m: -m["score"]):
193	            if m["feature"] not in seen and m["feature"] in self.ctx.features.index:
194	                seen.add(m["feature"])
195	                unique.append(m)
196	        return unique

204	    def _feedback_row(self, feature, model, market, policy):
205	        """(row, level) for the feature in model + market, or the model's all-market row if borrowing."""
206	        key = (feature, model, market)
207	        row = self.cells.loc[key] if key in self.cells.index else None
208	        n = int(row["n_comments"]) if row is not None else 0
209	        min_n = policy["scoring"]["min_comments_for_signal"]
210	        if n >= min_n:
211	            return row, "market", n
212	        b = policy["borrowing"]
213	        if b["enabled"] and (market != "CN" or b["into_cn"]) and (feature, model) in self.ctx.by_model.index:
214	            m = self.ctx.by_model.loc[(feature, model)]
215	            if m["n_comments"] >= min_n:
216	                return m, "borrowed", n
217	        return row, "none", n

220	        r, level, n_market = self._feedback_row(feature, model, market, policy)
221	        if r is None:
222	            return {"score": None, "status": f"no comments in {model} {market}", "n_comments": 0}
223	        ev = {"n_comments": int(r["n_comments"]), "n_comments_market": n_market, "level": level,
224	              "verdict": r["verdict"], "complaint_index": round(float(r["index_negative"]), 2),
225	              "ci_low": round(float(r["ci_low_negative"]), 2), "ci_high": round(float(min(r["ci_high_negative"], 99)), 2),
226	              "observed": int(r["obs_negative"]), "expected": round(float(r["exp_negative"]), 1)}
227	        if level == "none":
228	            return {**ev, "score": None,

230	                              f"(<{policy['scoring']['min_comments_for_signal']})"}
231	        status = "ok" if level == "market" else f"borrowed from {model} all markets ({n_market} in {market})"
232	        return {**ev, "score": policy["scoring"]["complaint_points"][r["verdict"]], "status": status}

250	    def _breadth(self, feature, model, market, policy):
251	        b = policy["borrowing"]
252	        if market == "CN" and not (b["enabled"] and b["into_cn"]):
253	            return {"score": None, "status": "no customer feedback from China in the data"}
254	        if model not in self.breadth_table.index.get_level_values(0):
255	            return {"score": None, "status": "no feedback for this model"}
256	        if (model, feature) not in self.breadth_table.index:
257	            return {"score": 0.0, "status": "ok", "n_comments": 0,
258	                    "model_comments": int(self.breadth_table.loc[model]["model_comments"].iloc[0])}

261	                "model_comments": int(r["model_comments"]), "share": round(float(r["share"]), 4),
262	                "rank_among_features": int(r["n_features"] - round(r["percentile"] * r["n_features"]) + 1),
263	                "n_features": int(r["n_features"])}

265	    def _survey(self, feature, model, market):
266	        if market == "CN":
267	            smodel, sheet = CN_SURVEY_MODEL.get(model), "CN_EU_2025 (China)"
268	        elif market == "EU":
269	            smodel, sheet = model, "CN_EU_2025 (EU)"
270	        elif market == "US":
271	            smodel, sheet = model, "US_2025"
272	        else:
273	            return {"score": None, "status": "no survey for Rest of World"}
274	        table = self._survey_rank.get((market, smodel))
275	        if table is None:
276	            return {"score": None, "status": f"no {market} survey for {model}"}
277	        mapping = taxonomy.US_SURVEY_TO_FEATURES if market == "US" else taxonomy.CN_EU_SURVEY_TO_FEATURES
278	        attrs = [a for a, fs in mapping.items() if feature in fs and a in table.index]
279	        if not attrs:
280	            return {"score": None, "status": "no matching survey attribute", "survey_model": smodel}
281	        rows = []
282	        for a in attrs:
283	            r = table.loc[a]
284	            weakness = (r["rank"] - 1) / (r["n"] - 1)
285	            row = {"attribute": a, "rank": int(r["rank"]), "of": int(r["n"]), "weakness": round(float(weakness), 3)}
286	            if market == "US":
287	                row.update(top2_box=round(float(r["top2_box"]), 3), bottom3_box=round(float(r["bottom3_box"]), 3),
288	                           model_mean_top2=round(float(r["overall_top2"]), 3))
289	            else:
290	                row.update(mean=round(float(r["mean"]), 2), model_mean=round(float(r["overall_mean"]), 2))
291	            rows.append(row)
292	        return {"score": round(float(np.mean([r["weakness"] for r in rows])), 3), "status": "ok",
293	                "sheet": sheet, "survey_model": smodel, "attributes": rows,
294	                "note": "CN survey covers the G68 (5 Series long wheelbase), not the G60" if smodel == "G68" else None}

296	    def _fitment(self, feature, model):
297	        summary = self.catalog.get("feature_fitment_summary")
298	        links = self.catalog.get("feature_option_links")
299	        if summary is None:
300	            return None
301	        s = summary[(summary["feature"] == feature) & (summary["model"] == model)]
302	        lk = links[(links["feature"] == feature) & (links["model"] == model)]
303	        listed_on = sorted(set(summary.loc[summary["feature"] == feature, "model"]) - {model})
304	        if s.empty:
305	            linked = feature in set(links["feature"])
306	            return {"tier": "not_listed" if linked else "no_link", "items": [], "listed_on": listed_on}
307	        r = s.iloc[0]
308	        return {"tier": r["tier"], "listed_on": listed_on, "n_variants": int(r["n_variants"]),
309	                "n_standard": int(r["n_standard"]),
310	                "n_optional": int(r["n_optional"]), "price_min_eur": _num(r["price_min_eur"]),
311	                "price_item": None if pd.isna(r["price_item"]) else r["price_item"],
312	                "price_via_package": None if pd.isna(r["price_via_package"]) else bool(r["price_via_package"]),
313	                "price_max_eur": _num(r["price_max_eur"]), "price_pct_of_base": _num(r["price_pct_of_base"]),
314	                "items": [{"name": x.option_name, "sa_code": None if pd.isna(x.sa_code) else x.sa_code,
315	                           "page": int(x.page), "matched_keyword": x.matched_keyword, "matched_in": x.matched_in}
316	                          for x in lk.itertuples()]}

318	    def _quotes(self, feature, model, market, n=2):
319	        lab = self.ctx.labels[(self.ctx.labels["feature"] == feature) & (self.ctx.labels["model"] == model)
320	                              & (self.ctx.labels["market"] == market)].drop_duplicates(["comment_id", "sentiment"])
321	        ids = sorted(lab["comment_id"].unique().tolist())
322	        merged = lab.merge(self.ctx.comments[["comment_id", "text", "n_labels", "n_words"]], on="comment_id")
323	        merged = merged[merged["n_words"] >= 6].assign(len_pen=lambda d: (d["text"].str.len() - 140).abs())
324	        merged = merged.sort_values(["n_labels", "len_pen"])
325	        quotes = [{"comment_id": r.comment_id, "sentiment": r.sentiment, "feedback_type": r.feedback_type,
326	                   "source": r.source, "country": r.country, "reason": r.reason, "text": r.text[:320]}
327	                  for r in merged.drop_duplicates("sentiment").head(n).itertuples()]
328	        return ids, quotes

330	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ evaluation
331	    def evaluate(self, idea: str = "", features=None, policy_overrides=None, models=None, markets=None) -> dict:
332	        policy = merge_policy(policy_overrides)
333	        resolution = self.resolve_idea(idea) if idea else None
334	        chosen = [f for f in (features or (resolution["suggested"] if resolution else [])) if f in self.ctx.features.index]
335	        models = [m for m in (models or config.MODELS) if m in config.MODELS]
336	        markets = [m for m in (markets or MARKETS) if m in MARKETS]
337	        result = {"idea": idea, "resolution": resolution, "features": [], "policy": policy,
338	                  "policy_hash": policy_hash(policy),
339	                  "data_hash": self.fingerprint["hash"], "models": models, "markets": markets}
340	        if not chosen:
341	            result["status"] = "no_direct_evidence" if resolution else "no_features"
342	            result["headline"] = (f"No feature in the feedback data matches '{idea}' directly. Related features "
343	                                  "are listed with their match scores; select one to evaluate it, or treat the "
344	                                  "idea as new (no customer evidence in this data).") if resolution else ""
345	            return result
346	        result["status"] = "ok"
347	        for feature in chosen:
348	            result["features"].append(self._evaluate_feature(feature, policy, models, markets))
349	        return result

351	    def _evaluate_feature(self, feature, policy, models, markets) -> dict:
352	        w = policy["weights"]
353	        th = policy["thresholds"]
354	        row = self.ctx.features.loc[feature]
355	        cells = []
356	        for model in models:
357	            fit = self._fitment(feature, model)
358	            for market in markets:
359	                vol = self._sales(model, market, policy["volume_year"])
360	                volume = vol.get(policy["volume_year"], 0.0)
361	                cell = {"model": model, "model_name": config.MODEL_NAMES[model], "market": market,
362	                        "market_name": MARKET_NAMES[market], "sales": vol, "volume": volume,
363	                        "sales_note": "5 Series volumes include the G68 long wheelbase" if model == "G60" else None}
364	                if sum(vol.values()) == 0:
365	                    cells.append({**cell, "recommendation": "Not sold", "score": None, "coverage": 0.0,
366	                                  "signals": {}, "reasons": [f"{model} has zero sales volume in {market} "
367	                                                             f"in sales_volumes.xlsx (2024, 2025, 2030)."],
368	                                  "action": None, "evidence": {}})
369	                    continue
370	                signals = {"complaints": self._complaints(feature, model, market, policy),
371	                           "breadth": self._breadth(feature, model, market, policy),
372	                           "requests": self._requests(feature, model, market, policy),
373	                           "survey": self._survey(feature, model, market)}
374	                disc = policy["borrowing"]["discount"]
375	                eff = {k: w[k] * (disc if signals[k].get("level") == "borrowed" else 1.0) for k in SIGNALS}
376	                avail = [k for k in SIGNALS if signals[k].get("score") is not None]
377	                total_w = sum(w[k] for k in SIGNALS)
378	                avail_w = sum(eff[k] for k in avail)
379	                coverage = avail_w / total_w if total_w else 0
380	                score = sum(eff[k] * signals[k]["score"] for k in avail) / avail_w if avail_w else None
381	                for k in SIGNALS:
382	                    signals[k]["weight"] = w[k]
383	                    signals[k]["effective_weight"] = round(eff[k], 4)
384	                    signals[k]["contribution"] = (round(eff[k] * signals[k]["score"] / avail_w, 4)
385	                                                  if k in avail and avail_w else None)
386	                if coverage < th["min_coverage"] or score is None:
387	                    rec = "Insufficient evidence"
388	                elif score >= th["prioritise"]:
389	                    rec = "Prioritise"
390	                elif score >= th["consider"]:
391	                    rec = "Consider"
392	                else:
393	                    rec = "Low priority"
394	                ids, quotes = self._quotes(feature, model, market)
395	                cell.update(signals=signals, score=None if score is None else round(score, 3),
396	                            coverage=round(coverage, 3), recommendation=rec,
397	                            market_weight=volume * policy["market_multipliers"][market],
398	                            action=_action(signals, fit, market),
399	                            reasons=_reasons(feature, model, market, signals, rec, coverage),
400	                            evidence={"comment_ids": ids[:40], "n_comment_ids": len(ids), "quotes": quotes})
401	                cells.append(cell)
402	        rollup = _rollup(cells, models)
403	        ladder = [{"model": m, **(self._fitment(feature, m) or {})} for m in config.MODELS]
404	        specs = self.catalog.get("feature_specs")
405	        spec_rows = [] if specs is None else [
406	            {"model": r.model, "variant": r.variant, "attribute": r.attribute, "value": r.value, "page": int(r.page)}
407	            for r in specs[specs["feature"] == feature].itertuples()]
408	        out = {"feature": feature, "domain": row["domain"], "umbrella": bool(row["is_umbrella"]),

499	def _rollup(cells, models) -> dict:

501	              ("Not sold", "Insufficient evidence")]

510	    return {"score": round(sum(c["score"] * c["market_weight"] for c in scored) / weight, 3) if weight else None,
