"""Validated competitor rows -> processed tables, the top-5 competitor sets and the quality report.

    python -m bmw_feedback competitors build        (also part of `all` when competitor-data/extracted exists)

Writes data/processed/competitor_*.csv and reports/competitor_quality.json. No network: it reads the extracted
rows, the saved source texts (to check every quote) and BMW's own processed price list.

Selection of the five competitors per BMW series x market (deterministic, recorded per row in `basis`):
    1. Models of the series' segment (registry.SERIES_SEGMENT) with a full-year sales figure in that market, from
       the (region, year) that covers the most of them (Europe-wide before Germany, 2025 before 2024); ranked by
       units. A source's own segment table is the evidence of who competes.
    2. If fewer than five, models that publishers name as rivals of that BMW (`rival` rows), from the fallback
       segments only, present in the market (a price or sales row there); ranked by the number of publishers.
    BMW series that are not sold in a market (zero volume in sales_volumes.xlsx) get no set.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from .. import config
from . import records, registry as R
from .snapshot import all_sources

P = config.PROCESSED_DIR
QUALITY_FILE = config.REPORTS_DIR / "competitor_quality.json"
TABLE_FILES = {name: P / f"competitor_{name}.csv" for name in
               ("models", "sets", "sales", "prices", "specs", "equipment", "reviews", "ratings", "rivals", "sources",
                "bmw_prices", "bmw_specs", "bmw_equipment")}

# BMW's own equipment, read from its DE price list: item key -> pattern on price-list item name / description /
# package contents (calibrated on catalog_option_items.csv; see the registry for what each item means)
BMW_ITEM_PATTERNS = {
    "hud": r"Head-Up", "acc": r"Driving Assistant Plus\b", "hands_off": r"Autobahnassistent|Autobahn- & City-Assistent",
    "pano_roof": r"Panorama[- ]?Glasdach", "massage": r"Massagefunktion vorn", "ventilated_seats": r"Sitzbelüftung vorn",
    "heated_wheel": r"Lenkradheizung", "surround_view": r"Surround View", "auto_parking": r"Parking Assistant",
    "wireless_charging": r"Wireless Charging", "premium_audio": r"harman|Bowers", "ambient_light": r"Ambientes? Licht",
    "keyless": r"Komfortzugang", "power_tailgate": r"Heckklappenbetätigung", "soft_close": r"Soft-Close",
    "auto_doors": r"Automatiktür", "rear_entertainment": r"Theatre Screen|Theater Screen", "air_suspension": r"Luftfeder",
    "rear_steering": r"Integral-Aktivlenkung",
    "matrix_lights": r"Adaptiver LED-Scheinwerfer|Kristallscheinwerfer|Laserlicht", "dashcam": r"Drive Recorder",
    "digital_key": r"Digital Key",
}
BMW_SPEC_KEYS = {   # spec attribute -> (technical attribute_key(s), which bound of a range: min | max)
    "torque_nm": (["drehmoment in nm"], "min"),
    "accel_0_100_s": (["beschleunigung 0–100 km / h in s"], "min"),
    "top_speed_kmh": (["höchstgeschwindigkeit in km / h", "höchstgeschwindigkeit elektr. in km / h"], "max"),
    "boot_l": (["gepäckraumvolumen in l"], "min"),
    "range_km_wltp": (["elektrische reichweite, wltp in km"], "max"),
    "battery_kwh_net": (["energieinhalt batterie in kwh, netto"], "min"),
    "dc_charge_kw": (["maximale ladeleistung dc in kw"], "max"),
}
SENTIMENT_OF_KIND = {"expert_pro": "positive", "expert_con": "negative"}
REGION_PREFERENCE = {"EU": ["Europe", "Germany"], "US": ["United States"], "CN": ["China"], "RoW": ["Australia"]}


class CompetitorDataError(ValueError):
    """Extracted rows failed validation; the build writes nothing."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def _frame(rows: list[dict], cols: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.DataFrame([{c: r.get(c) for c in cols} for r in rows], columns=cols)
    return df


def _publisher(sid: str, metas: dict) -> str | None:
    m = metas.get(sid)
    return m["publisher"] if m else None


def _region_key(market: str, region: str) -> int:
    prefs = REGION_PREFERENCE.get(market, [])
    low = (region or "").lower()
    for i, p in enumerate(prefs):
        if p.lower() in low:
            return i
    return len(prefs)


def bmw_sold(series: str, market: str) -> bool:
    sales = pd.read_csv(P / "sales.csv")
    group = {"F70": "F70", "G60": "G60_G68", "G70": "G70"}[series]
    s = sales[(sales["model_group"] == group) & (sales["market_code"] == market)]
    return bool(s["volume"].sum() > 0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- BMW side (official data)
def bmw_tables() -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """BMW entry prices, specs and equipment from the DE price list already parsed by option_catalog."""
    from .. import option_catalog
    var = pd.read_csv(P / "catalog_variants.csv")
    tech = pd.read_csv(P / "catalog_technical.csv")
    prices = []
    for m, g in var.groupby("model"):
        g = g.sort_values("base_price_eur")
        cheapest = g.iloc[0]
        for engine, ge in g.groupby("engine"):
            r = ge.iloc[0]
            prices.append({"model": m, "variant": r["variant"], "powertrain": r["engine"], "power_kw": r["power_kw"],
                           "amount": r["base_price_eur"], "page": int(r["page"]), "entry": r["variant"] == cheapest["variant"],
                           "ref": f"{m}_OptionList.PDF"})
    specs = []
    for r in var.itertuples():
        specs.append({"model": r.model, "variant": r.variant, "powertrain": r.engine, "attribute": "power_kw",
                      "value": r.power_kw, "page": int(r.page)})
    engines = dict(zip(zip(var["model"], var["variant"]), var["engine"]))
    for attr, (keys, bound) in BMW_SPEC_KEYS.items():
        t = tech[tech["attribute_key"].isin(keys)].copy()
        if attr in ("range_km_wltp", "battery_kwh_net", "dc_charge_kw"):        # electric data: BEVs only
            t = t[[engines.get((m, v)) == "BEV" for m, v in zip(t["model"], t["variant"])]]
        t = t.dropna(subset=["value_min" if bound == "min" else "value_max"])
        t = t.drop_duplicates(["model", "variant"])
        for r in t.itertuples():
            specs.append({"model": r.model, "variant": r.variant, "powertrain": engines.get((r.model, r.variant)),
                          "attribute": attr, "value": float(r.value_min if bound == "min" else r.value_max),
                          "page": int(r.page)})
    cat = {k: pd.read_csv(P / f"catalog_{k}.csv") for k in ("option_items", "fitment", "variants")}
    items = cat["option_items"][cat["option_items"]["page_type"].isin(option_catalog.LINK_PAGE_TYPES)]
    links = []
    for key, pat in BMW_ITEM_PATTERNS.items():
        rx = re.compile(pat, re.I)
        for it in items.itertuples():
            parts = [("name", it.name)]
            parts += [("description", d) for d in str(it.description or "").split(" | ") if d and d != "nan"]
            parts += [("contents", c) for c in str(it.contents or "").split(" | ") if c and c != "nan"]
            hit = next(((where, text) for where, text in parts if rx.search(str(text))), None)
            if hit:
                links.append({"feature": key, "model": it.model, "item_id": it.item_id, "option_name": it.name,
                              "sa_code": it.sa_code, "page": it.page, "page_type": it.page_type,
                              "matched_in": hit[0], "matched_text": hit[1]})
    links = pd.DataFrame(links, columns=["feature", "model", "item_id", "option_name", "sa_code", "page", "page_type",
                                         "matched_in", "matched_text"])
    fv = option_catalog.feature_fitment(links, cat)
    summ = option_catalog.fitment_summary(fv) if len(fv) else pd.DataFrame()
    equip = []
    for key in R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS:
        for m in config.MODELS:
            s = summ[(summ["feature"] == key) & (summ["model"] == m)] if len(summ) else summ
            lk = links[(links["feature"] == key) & (links["model"] == m)]
            if s is None or s.empty:
                equip.append({"model": m, "item": key, "tier": "not_listed", "n_variants": None, "n_standard": None,
                              "n_optional": None, "price_min_eur": None, "price_item": None, "via_package": None,
                              "items": "", "pages": ""})
                continue
            r = s.iloc[0]
            equip.append({"model": m, "item": key, "tier": r["tier"], "n_variants": int(r["n_variants"]),
                          "n_standard": int(r["n_standard"]), "n_optional": int(r["n_optional"]),
                          "price_min_eur": None if pd.isna(r["price_min_eur"]) else float(r["price_min_eur"]),
                          "price_item": None if pd.isna(r["price_item"]) else r["price_item"],
                          "via_package": None if pd.isna(r["price_via_package"]) else bool(r["price_via_package"]),
                          "items": " | ".join(sorted(set(lk["option_name"]))),
                          "pages": " | ".join(str(int(p)) for p in sorted(set(lk["page"])))})
    return {"bmw_prices": pd.DataFrame(prices), "bmw_specs": pd.DataFrame(specs), "bmw_equipment": pd.DataFrame(equip)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- selection
def select_sets(models: pd.DataFrame, sales: pd.DataFrame, rivals: pd.DataFrame, prices: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    seg = dict(zip(models["model_id"], models["segment"]))
    rows = []
    fy = sales[(sales["period"] == "FY") & sales["preferred"]] if len(sales) else sales
    for series in config.MODELS:
        segment = R.SERIES_SEGMENT[series]
        for market in R.MARKETS:
            base = {"series": series, "market": market}
            if not bmw_sold(series, market):
                rows.append({**base, "rank": None, "model_id": None, "basis": "not_sold",
                             "note": f"BMW sells no {series} in {R.MARKET_NAMES[market]} (sales_volumes.xlsx)"})
                continue
            cand = fy[(fy["market"] == market) & (fy["model_id"].map(seg) == segment)
                      & ~fy["model_id"].isin(R.SELF_SERIES) & (fy["units"] > 0)] if len(fy) else fy
            chosen = []
            if len(cand):
                cover = cand.groupby(["region", "year"])["model_id"].nunique().reset_index(name="n")
                cover["rk"] = [_region_key(market, r) for r in cover["region"]]
                cover = cover.sort_values(["n", "rk", "year"], ascending=[False, True, False])
                region, year = cover.iloc[0]["region"], int(cover.iloc[0]["year"])
                pick = cand[(cand["region"] == region) & (cand["year"] == year)]
                pick = pick.sort_values(["units", "tier_rank"], ascending=[False, True]).drop_duplicates("model_id")
                for r in pick.head(R.N_COMPETITORS).itertuples():
                    chosen.append({**base, "model_id": r.model_id, "basis": "sales", "units": int(r.units),
                                   "year": year, "region": region, "sales_source_id": r.source_id,
                                   "segment_label": r.segment_label, "n_rival_mentions": None,
                                   "note": None})
            if len(chosen) < R.N_COMPETITORS and len(rivals):
                present = set(prices.loc[prices["market"] == market, "model_id"]) | set(
                    sales.loc[sales["market"] == market, "model_id"])
                allowed = set(R.FALLBACK_SEGMENTS[series])
                rv = rivals[(rivals["bmw_series"] == series) & (rivals["market"].isna() | (rivals["market"] == market))]
                rv = rv[rv["model_id"].map(seg).isin(allowed) & rv["model_id"].isin(present)
                        & ~rv["model_id"].isin([c["model_id"] for c in chosen]) & ~rv["model_id"].isin(R.SELF_SERIES)]
                ranked = (rv.groupby("model_id")["publisher"].nunique().reset_index(name="n")
                          .assign(seg_order=lambda d: d["model_id"].map(lambda m: R.FALLBACK_SEGMENTS[series].index(seg[m])))
                          .sort_values(["n", "seg_order", "model_id"], ascending=[False, True, True]))
                for r in ranked.itertuples():
                    if len(chosen) >= R.N_COMPETITORS:
                        break
                    chosen.append({**base, "model_id": r.model_id, "basis": "rival_mentions", "units": None,
                                   "year": None, "region": None, "sales_source_id": None, "segment_label": None,
                                   "n_rival_mentions": int(r.n),
                                   "note": f"named as a {series} rival by {int(r.n)} publisher(s); no same-segment "
                                           "sales figure for this market"})
            if not chosen:
                rows.append({**base, "rank": None, "model_id": None, "basis": "no_data",
                             "note": "no sales figures or rival mentions found for this market"})
            for i, c in enumerate(chosen, start=1):
                rows.append({**c, "rank": i})
    cols = ["series", "market", "rank", "model_id", "basis", "units", "year", "region", "sales_source_id",
            "segment_label", "n_rival_mentions", "note"]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).reindex(columns=cols)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- reviews
def classify_reviews(reviews: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if reviews.empty:
        return reviews.assign(pred_feedback_type=None, pred_feedback_type_p=None, pred_domain=None, pred_domain_p=None,
                              pred_feature=None, pred_feature_p=None, sentiment=None, sentiment_basis=None)
    from ..classifier import predict
    preds = predict(reviews["text"].tolist())
    out = reviews.copy()
    out["pred_feedback_type"] = [p["feedback_type"][0][0] for p in preds]
    out["pred_feedback_type_p"] = [p["feedback_type"][0][1] for p in preds]
    out["pred_domain"] = [p["domain"][0][0] for p in preds]
    out["pred_domain_p"] = [p["domain"][0][1] for p in preds]
    out["pred_feature"] = [p["feature"][0][0] for p in preds]
    out["pred_feature_p"] = [p["feature"][0][1] for p in preds]
    sent, basis = [], []
    for kind, ft in zip(out["kind"], out["pred_feedback_type"]):
        if kind in SENTIMENT_OF_KIND:
            sent.append(SENTIMENT_OF_KIND[kind])
            basis.append("pros/cons list")
        else:
            sent.append(config.SENTIMENT.get(ft, "positive"))
            basis.append("feedback-type classifier")
    out["sentiment"], out["sentiment_basis"] = sent, basis
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- build
def build(drop_invalid: bool = False, require_snapshot: bool = True) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    rows, load_errors = records.load()
    valid, errors, stats = records.validate_all(rows, require_snapshot=require_snapshot)
    errors = load_errors + errors
    if errors and not drop_invalid:
        raise CompetitorDataError(f"{len(errors)} invalid competitor row(s); fix them or build with --drop-invalid:\n"
                                  + "\n".join(errors[:40]))
    if errors:                                   # rows named in a cross-row error are dropped as well
        bad = {e.split(" ", 1)[0].rstrip(":") for e in errors}
        valid = [r for r in valid if r["_where"] not in bad]
    metas = {m["source_id"]: m for m in all_sources()}
    by = {t: [r for r in valid if r["table"] == t] for t in R.TABLES}
    for r in valid:
        r["publisher"] = _publisher(r.get("source_id"), metas)

    models = _frame(by["model"], ["model_id", "brand", "model", "segment", "body", "generation"]).drop_duplicates("model_id")
    models["name"] = models["brand"] + " " + models["model"]
    models["is_bmw"] = models["model_id"].isin(R.SELF_SERIES)
    models["bmw_series"] = models["model_id"].map(R.SELF_SERIES)
    models = models.sort_values(["segment", "model_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    sales = _frame(by["sales"], ["model_id", "market", "region", "year", "period", "units", "basis", "tier",
                                 "segment_label", "source_id", "publisher", "evidence", "note"])
    sales["period"] = sales["period"].fillna("FY")
    sales["tier_rank"] = sales["tier"].map(R.TIER_RANK)
    # several sources for the same figure: the most authoritative one is preferred; disagreements are reported
    sales = sales.sort_values(["model_id", "market", "region", "year", "period", "tier_rank", "source_id"])
    key = ["model_id", "market", "region", "year", "period"]
    sales["preferred"] = ~sales.duplicated(key)
    conflicts = []
    for k, g in sales.groupby(key):
        if g["units"].nunique() > 1:
            conflicts.append({"key": dict(zip(key, [str(x) for x in k])),
                              "values": [{"units": int(r.units), "source_id": r.source_id, "tier": r.tier}
                                         for r in g.itertuples()]})

    prices = _frame(by["price"], ["model_id", "market", "country", "currency", "variant", "amount", "powertrain",
                                  "price_type", "tax_basis", "entry", "model_year", "as_of", "power_kw", "source_id",
                                  "publisher", "evidence", "note"])
    prices["entry"] = prices["entry"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
    specs = _frame(by["spec"], ["model_id", "variant", "attribute", "value", "unit", "powertrain", "market",
                                "source_id", "publisher", "evidence", "note"])
    equipment = _frame(by["equipment"], ["model_id", "country", "item", "status", "price_eur", "item_name",
                                         "variant_scope", "source_id", "publisher", "evidence", "note"])
    equipment["feature"] = equipment["item"].map(lambda k: R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS[k]["feature"])
    reviews = _frame(by["review"], ["model_id", "market", "country", "kind", "text", "rating", "rating_scale", "date",
                                    "model_year", "source_id", "publisher", "note"])
    reviews = classify_reviews(reviews)
    ratings = _frame(by["rating"], ["model_id", "market", "country", "rating_kind", "score", "scale_max", "n_reviews",
                                    "model_year", "source_id", "publisher", "evidence", "note"])
    rivals = _frame(by["rival"], ["model_id", "bmw_series", "market", "source_id", "publisher", "evidence"])
    used = sorted({r["source_id"] for r in valid if r.get("source_id")})
    sources = pd.DataFrame([{k: metas[s].get(k) for k in ("source_id", "url", "final_url", "publisher", "title",
                                                          "retrieved_at", "kind", "rendered", "sha256", "bytes")}
                            for s in used if s in metas])

    sets = select_sets(models, sales, rivals, prices)
    tables = {"models": models, "sets": sets, "sales": sales.drop(columns=["tier_rank"]), "prices": prices,
              "specs": specs, "equipment": equipment, "reviews": reviews, "ratings": ratings, "rivals": rivals,
              "sources": sources, **bmw_tables()}
    quality = _quality(tables, stats, errors, conflicts, drop_invalid)
    return tables, quality


def _coverage(tables: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Per competitor in each set: which kinds of data exist for its market."""
    out = []
    t = tables
    for r in t["sets"].dropna(subset=["model_id"]).itertuples():
        ref = R.REFERENCE[r.market]
        out.append({"series": r.series, "market": r.market, "rank": int(r.rank), "model_id": r.model_id,
                    "price": bool(((t["prices"]["model_id"] == r.model_id) & (t["prices"]["country"] == ref["country"])).any()),
                    "sales": bool(((t["sales"]["model_id"] == r.model_id) & (t["sales"]["market"] == r.market)).any()),
                    "specs": int((t["specs"]["model_id"] == r.model_id).sum()),
                    "equipment_items": int((t["equipment"]["model_id"] == r.model_id).sum()),
                    "reviews": int(((t["reviews"]["model_id"] == r.model_id) & (t["reviews"]["market"] == r.market)).sum()),
                    "ratings": int(((t["ratings"]["model_id"] == r.model_id) & (t["ratings"]["market"] == r.market)).sum())})
    return out


def data_hash(tables: dict) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in sorted(tables):
        h.update(name.encode() + tables[name].to_csv(index=False).encode())
    return h.hexdigest()[:12]


def _quality(tables: dict, stats: dict, errors: list, conflicts: list, dropped: bool) -> dict:
    sets = tables["sets"]
    retrieved = sorted(tables["sources"]["retrieved_at"].dropna()) if len(tables["sources"]) else []
    return {
        "built_at": pd.Timestamp.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
        "data_hash": data_hash(tables),
        "records": {**stats, "dropped_invalid": len(errors) if dropped else 0},
        "invalid_rows": errors[:200],
        "sales_conflicts": conflicts,
        "tables": {k: int(len(v)) for k, v in tables.items()},
        "sources": {"n": int(len(tables["sources"])), "retrieved_from": retrieved[0] if retrieved else None,
                    "retrieved_to": retrieved[-1] if retrieved else None,
                    "publishers": tables["sources"]["publisher"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(tables["sources"]) else {}},
        "sets": [{"series": s, "market": m, "status": g["basis"].iloc[0] if g["model_id"].isna().all() else "ok",
                  "competitors": [x for x in g["model_id"].dropna()],
                  "basis": sorted(set(g["basis"].dropna()))}
                 for (s, m), g in sets.groupby(["series", "market"], sort=False)],
        "coverage": _coverage(tables),
        "checks": {"sets_at_most_five": bool((sets.groupby(["series", "market"])["model_id"].count() <= R.N_COMPETITORS).all()),
                   "no_duplicate_competitor_in_a_set": not sets.dropna(subset=["model_id"]).duplicated(["series", "market", "model_id"]).any(),
                   "every_sold_tuple_has_a_set_or_reason": bool(len(sets.groupby(["series", "market"])) == len(config.MODELS) * len(R.MARKETS)),
                   "one_currency_per_reference_country": _one_currency(tables["prices"])},
    }


def _one_currency(prices: pd.DataFrame) -> bool:
    for market, ref in R.REFERENCE.items():
        p = prices[(prices["market"] == market) & (prices["country"] == ref["country"])]
        if len(p) and set(p["currency"]) != {ref["currency"]}:
            return False
    return True


def save(tables: dict, quality: dict) -> None:
    P.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for name, df in tables.items():
        df.to_csv(TABLE_FILES[name], index=False)
    QUALITY_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(quality, indent=1, default=_json_default, ensure_ascii=False))


def _json_default(o):
    if isinstance(o, (np.integer,)):
        return int(o)
    if isinstance(o, (np.floating,)):
        return float(o)
    if isinstance(o, (np.bool_,)):
        return bool(o)
    return str(o)


def build_and_save(drop_invalid: bool = False) -> dict:
    tables, quality = build(drop_invalid=drop_invalid)
    failed = [k for k, v in quality["checks"].items() if not v]
    if failed:
        raise CompetitorDataError(f"competitor checks failed: {failed}")
    save(tables, quality)
    return quality


def load_tables() -> dict | None:
    """The processed competitor tables, or None if they were never built."""
    if not all(f.exists() for f in TABLE_FILES.values()):
        return None
    out = {}
    for name, f in TABLE_FILES.items():
        try:
            out[name] = pd.read_csv(f, keep_default_na=False, na_values=[""])
        except pd.errors.EmptyDataError:
            out[name] = pd.DataFrame()
    return out


def load_quality() -> dict | None:
    return json.loads(QUALITY_FILE.read_text()) if QUALITY_FILE.exists() else None

input.content:
"""The competitor comparison as facts: stable ID, a deterministic sentence, the value and where it comes from.

The competitor analyst and presenter agents may use only these facts. Every derived number a manager would ask
for (price gaps in money and percent, ranks, sales differences, equipment counts) is already in a statement, so
the agents never compute. Provenance points to the knowledge-graph node of the row (competitor nodes are added
by graph/build.py) and to the saved web source.
"""

import hashlib
import json

from ..agents.contracts import Fact, FactBundle, Provenance
from . import registry as R

PT_SLUG = {"combustion": "ice", "plug-in hybrid": "phev", "electric": "bev"}
PT_TEXT = {"combustion": "combustion (incl. mild and full hybrid)", "plug-in hybrid": "plug-in hybrid",
           "electric": "electric"}
STATUS_TEXT = {"standard": "standard", "standard_some": "standard on some versions", "optional": "a paid option",
               "package": "available only in a package", "not_available": "not offered",
               "unknown": "not found in the collected data", "not_listed": "not found in BMW's DE price list"}
KIND_TEXT = {"owner_review": "owner review", "expert_pro": "expert pro", "expert_con": "expert con",
             "expert_verdict": "expert verdict"}


def competition_id(scope: dict, data_hash: str) -> str:
    payload = json.dumps({"scope": scope, "data": data_hash}, sort_keys=True)
    return "cx" + hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:14]


def money(amount: float, currency: str) -> str:
    return f"{R.CURRENCY_SYMBOL.get(currency, currency)} {amount:,.0f}"


def _rng(spec: dict) -> str:
    unit = spec["unit"]
    fmt = (lambda v: f"{v:,.1f}") if unit in ("s", "kWh") else (lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}")
    return f"{fmt(spec['min'])} {unit}" if spec["min"] == spec["max"] else f"{fmt(spec['min'])}-{fmt(spec['max'])} {unit}"


def _pct_word(gap: dict) -> str:
    return "the same as" if gap["direction"] == "equal" else f"{abs(gap['pct']):.1f}% {gap['direction']}"


class CompetitorFactBuilder:
    def __init__(self, comparison: dict, graph=None, cid: str = ""):
        self.c, self.g, self.cid = comparison, graph, cid
        self.facts: list[Fact] = []
        self._ids: set = set()
        self.missing_nodes: list[str] = []

    def _node(self, node: str | None) -> str | None:
        if node is None or self.g is None:
            return node
        if node in self.g:
            return node
        self.missing_nodes.append(node)
        return None

    def add(self, fid, group, statement, value=None, *, node=None, kind="web", ref="", key=None, page=None, unit=None,
            feature=None, series=None, market=None):
        if fid in self._ids:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate competitor fact id {fid}")
        self._ids.add(fid)
        self.facts.append(Fact(id=fid, group=group, statement=statement, value=value, unit=unit, feature=feature,
                               series=series, market=market,
                               source=Provenance(node_id=self._node(node), kind=kind, ref=ref, key=key, page=page)))

    @staticmethod
    def _src(src: dict | None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
        if not src:
            return "", None
        return src.get("url") or src.get("ref") or "", src.get("retrieved_at")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ build
    def build(self) -> FactBundle:
        c = self.c
        self.add("cx.data", "data", f"Competitor data version {c['data_hash']}: public web sources retrieved between "
                 f"{(c.get('retrieved_from') or '')[:10]} and {(c.get('retrieved_to') or '')[:10]}.", c["data_hash"],
                 kind="derived", ref="data/processed/competitor_sources.csv")
        for cv in c["caveats"]:
            self.add(f"cx.caveat.{cv['id']}", "caveat", cv["text"], None, kind="derived",
                     ref="bmw_feedback/competitors/engine.py")
        for f in c.get("features_without_items", []):
            slug = "".join(ch if ch.isalnum() else "_" for ch in f.lower()).strip("_")
            self.add(f"cx.noitem.{slug}", "equipment", f"Competitor equipment was not collected for '{f}': it is not "
                     "one of the compared equipment items.", f, kind="config", ref="competitors/registry.py",
                     feature=f, node=f"feature:{f}")
        for t in c["tuples"]:
            self._tuple(t)
        return FactBundle(evaluation_id=self.cid, idea="competitor analysis", facts=self.facts)

    def _tuple(self, t: dict):
        s, m = t["series"], t["market"]
        p = f"cx.{s}.{m}"
        where = f"the {t['series_name']} in {t['market_name']}"
        if t["status"] != "ok":
            text = (f"The {t['series_name']} is 'Not sold' in {t['market_name']} (zero volume in sales_volumes.xlsx), "
                    "so it has no competitor set there." if t["status"] == "not_sold" else
                    f"No competitor set could be formed for {where}: {t.get('note')}.")
            self.add(f"{p}.status", "set", text, "Not sold" if t["status"] == "not_sold" else "no data",
                     node=f"series:{s}", kind="derived", ref="competitors/build.py select_sets", series=s, market=m)
            return
        comps, bmw, ref = t["competitors"], t["bmw"], t["reference"]
        listing = "; ".join(f"{c['rank']}. {c['name']}" + (f" ({c['selection']['units']:,} units)"
                                                          if c["selection"]["units"] is not None else "")
                            for c in comps)
        self.add(f"{p}.set", "set", f"Top {len(comps)} competitors of {where} ({t['selection_rule']}): {listing}.",
                 len(comps), node=f"series:{s}", kind="derived", ref="data/processed/competitor_sets.csv",
                 key=f"{s}|{m}", series=s, market=m)
        self._bmw(p, t)
        for c in comps:
            self._competitor(p, t, c)
        self._summary(p, t)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ BMW
    def _bmw(self, p, t):
        s, m, bmw, ref = t["series"], t["market"], t["bmw"], t["reference"]
        e = bmw["entry"]
        name, country = t["series_name"], ref["country_name"]
        if e:
            if m == "EU":
                self.add(f"{p}.bmw.entry", "price", f"Entry price of the {name} in Germany: {money(e['amount'], 'EUR')} "
                         f"({e['variant']}, BMW DE price list July 2026, incl. 19% VAT).", e["amount"], unit="EUR",
                         node=f"variant:{s}|{e['variant']}", kind="pdf", ref=e["source"]["ref"], page=e["source"]["page"],
                         series=s, market=m)
            else:
                url, at = self._src(e["source"])
                self.add(f"{p}.bmw.entry", "price", f"Entry price of the {name} in {country}: "
                         f"{money(e['amount'], e['currency'])} ({e['variant']}, {e['tax_basis']}, "
                         f"{e['source'].get('publisher')}).", e["amount"], unit=e["currency"],
                         node=f"cprice:{e['row_id']}", ref=url, key=at, series=s, market=m)
        else:
            self.add(f"{p}.bmw.entry", "price", f"No {country} price for the {name} was found in the collected data, "
                     "so prices cannot be compared in this market.", None, node=f"series:{s}", kind="derived",
                     ref="data/processed/competitor_prices.csv", series=s, market=m)
        for r in bmw["reviews"].get("quotes", []):
            pass
        self._ratings_own(p, t)
        self._reviews(f"{p}.bmw", t, bmw, name)
        for k, eq in bmw["equipment"].items():
            label = R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS[k]["label"]
            st = eq["status"]
            text = f"{label} on the {name} (BMW DE price list, July 2026): "
            if st in ("standard", "standard_some", "optional"):
                text += {"standard": f"standard on all {eq['n_variants']} variants in the equipment tables",
                         "standard_some": f"standard on {eq['n_standard']} of {eq['n_variants']} variants, optional on "
                                          f"{eq['n_optional']}",
                         "optional": f"optional on {eq['n_optional']} of {eq['n_variants']} variants"}[st]
                if eq.get("price_eur"):
                    text += (f"; cheapest way to get it: '{eq['price_item']}' from {money(eq['price_eur'], 'EUR')}"
                             + (" (a package with other equipment)" if eq.get("via_package") else ""))
                text += "."
            else:
                text += "no item in the price list matched (it may be missing from the price list or named differently)."
            node = f"option:{eq['item_id']}" if eq.get("item_id") else f"series:{s}"
            self.add(f"{p}.bmw.eq.{k}", "equipment", text, st, node=node, kind="pdf", ref=f"{s}_OptionList.PDF",
                     feature=R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS[k]["feature"], series=s, market=m)

    def _ratings_own(self, p, t):
        s, m, name = t["series"], t["market"], t["series_name"]
        for j, r in enumerate(t["bmw"]["ratings"], start=1):
            url, at = self._src(r["source"])
            n = f" from {int(r['n_reviews']):,} reviews" if r.get("n_reviews") else ""
            self.add(f"{p}.bmw.rating{j}", "rating", f"{r['publisher']} {r['kind'].replace('_', ' ')} for the {name}: "
                     f"{r['score']:g} of {r['scale_max']:g}{n}.", r["score"], node=f"crating:{r['row_id']}", ref=url,
                     key=at, series=s, market=m)

    def _reviews(self, fid, t, entity, name):
        s, m = t["series"], t["market"]
        rv = entity["reviews"]
        if not rv.get("n"):
            return
        top = lambda xs: ", ".join(f"{d} ({n})" for d, n in xs) or "none"
        self.add(f"{fid}.reviews", "reviews", f"Review statements about the {name} in {t['market_name']} "
                 f"({', '.join(rv['publishers'])}): {rv['n']} classified, {rv['positive']} praise and {rv['negative']} "
                 f"criticism; most-praised topics: {top(rv['top_praise'])}; most-criticised topics: "
                 f"{top(rv['top_criticism'])}.", rv["n"], kind="derived",
                 node=f"competitor:{entity['model_id']}" if entity["model_id"] not in R.SELF_SERIES else f"series:{s}",
                 ref="data/processed/competitor_reviews.csv (feedback-type and domain classifiers)", series=s, market=m)
        for d, counts in rv.get("in_domain", {}).items():
            slug = "".join(ch if ch.isalnum() else "_" for ch in d.lower()).strip("_")
            self.add(f"{fid}.reviews.{slug}", "reviews", f"Review statements about the {name} in {t['market_name']} "
                     f"on the topic '{d}': {counts['positive']} praise, {counts['negative']} criticism.",
                     counts["negative"], kind="derived",
                     node=f"competitor:{entity['model_id']}" if entity["model_id"] not in R.SELF_SERIES else f"series:{s}",
                     ref="data/processed/competitor_reviews.csv", series=s, market=m)
        for j, q in enumerate(rv.get("quotes", []), start=1):
            url, at = self._src(q["source"])
            pub = (q["source"] or {}).get("publisher")
            self.add(f"{fid}.quote{j}", "quote", f"{KIND_TEXT[q['kind']].capitalize()} on the {name} ({pub}): "
                     f"\"{q['text']}\"", q["text"], node=f"creview:{q['row_id']}", ref=url, key=at, series=s, market=m)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ one competitor
    def _competitor(self, p, t, c):
        s, m, ref, bmw = t["series"], t["market"], t["reference"], t["bmw"]
        k = f"{p}.c{c['rank']}"
        name, bname, country = c["name"], t["series_name"], ref["country_name"]
        node = f"competitor:{c['model_id']}"
        sel = c["selection"]
        if c["basis"] == "sales":
            url, at = self._src(sel["source"])
            seg = f" (segment '{sel['segment_label']}')" if sel.get("segment_label") else ""
            text = (f"Competitor {c['rank']} of the {bname} in {t['market_name']}: {name}, with {sel['units']:,} "
                    f"units sold in {sel['region']} in {sel['year']}{seg}, source {(sel['source'] or {}).get('publisher')}.")
            self.add(k, "set", text, c["rank"], node=node, ref=url, key=at, series=s, market=m)
        else:
            self.add(k, "set", f"Competitor {c['rank']} of the {bname} in {t['market_name']}: {name}, {sel['note']}.",
                     c["rank"], node=node, kind="derived", ref="data/processed/competitor_rivals.csv", series=s, market=m)
        e = c["entry"]
        if e and c["gap"]:
            g = c["gap"]
            url, at = self._src(e["source"])
            rel = ("the same as" if g["direction"] == "equal" else
                   f"{money(abs(g['abs']), e['currency'])} ({abs(g['pct']):.1f}%) {g['direction']}")
            self.add(f"{k}.entry", "price", f"Entry price of the {name} in {country}: {money(e['amount'], e['currency'])}"
                     f" ({e['variant']}, {e['tax_basis']}, {e['source'].get('publisher')}); that is {rel} the {bname} "
                     f"entry price of {money(bmw['entry']['amount'], e['currency'])}.", e["amount"], unit=e["currency"],
                     node=f"cprice:{e['row_id']}", ref=url, key=at, series=s, market=m)
        elif e:
            url, at = self._src(e["source"])
            self.add(f"{k}.entry", "price", f"Entry price of the {name} in {country}: {money(e['amount'], e['currency'])}"
                     f" ({e['variant']}, {e['tax_basis']}); not comparable with the {bname} price in the data "
                     "(different price basis or no BMW price).", e["amount"], unit=e["currency"],
                     node=f"cprice:{e['row_id']}", ref=url, key=at, series=s, market=m)
        else:
            self.add(f"{k}.entry", "price", f"No {country} price for the {name} was found in the collected data.", None,
                     node=node, kind="derived", ref="data/processed/competitor_prices.csv", series=s, market=m)
        for row in c["by_powertrain"]:
            if not (row["competitor"] and row["bmw"] and row["gap"]):
                continue
            cp, bp, g = row["competitor"], row["bmw"], row["gap"]
            if e and cp["row_id"] == e["row_id"] and bmw["entry"] and bp["variant"] == bmw["entry"]["variant"]:
                continue                                      # same pair as the entry-price fact
            url, at = self._src(cp["source"])
            rel = ("the same as" if g["direction"] == "equal" else
                   f"{money(abs(g['abs']), cp['currency'])} ({abs(g['pct']):.1f}%) {g['direction']}")
            self.add(f"{k}.price.{PT_SLUG[row['group']]}", "price", f"Cheapest {PT_TEXT[row['group']]} version in "
                     f"{country}: {name} {cp['variant']} at {money(cp['amount'], cp['currency'])}, {rel} the {bname} "
                     f"{bp['variant']} at {money(bp['amount'], bp['currency'])}.", cp["amount"], unit=cp["currency"],
                     node=f"cprice:{cp['row_id']}", ref=url, key=at, series=s, market=m)
        if c["sales"]:
            sa = c["sales"]
            url, at = self._src(sa["source"])
            text = f"{name}: {sa['units']:,} units sold in {sa['region']} in {sa['year']}"
            if c["sales_vs_bmw"] and c["bmw_sales"]:
                v, b = c["sales_vs_bmw"], c["bmw_sales"]
                word = "more" if v["abs"] > 0 else "fewer" if v["abs"] < 0 else "the same number of"
                same = "same source" if v["same_source"] else "same region and year, different source"
                text += (f", vs {b['units']:,} for the {bname} ({same}): {abs(v['abs']):,} ({abs(v['pct']):.1f}%) "
                         f"{word}" if v["abs"] else f", the same as the {bname} ({same})")
            self.add(f"{k}.sales", "sales", text + ".", sa["units"], unit="units", node=f"csales:{sa['row_id']}",
                     ref=url, key=at, series=s, market=m)
        for attr, sp in c["specs"].items():
            b = bmw["specs"].get(attr)
            text = f"{sp['label']}: {name} {_rng(sp)} across {sp['n']} recorded value(s)"
            text += f" vs {bname} {_rng(b)}." if b else f"; no comparable {bname} value in the data."
            node_id = f"cspec:{sp['row_ids'][0]}" if sp.get("row_ids") else node
            self.add(f"{k}.spec.{attr}", "spec", text, sp["max"], unit=sp["unit"], node=node_id, kind="web",
                     ref="; ".join(sp["sources"]), series=s, market=m)
        for item, eq in c["equipment"].items():
            label = R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS[item]["label"]
            st = eq["status"]
            text = f"{label} on the {name} (German market): {STATUS_TEXT[st]}"
            if st == "standard_some" and eq.get("variant_scope"):
                text += f" ({eq['variant_scope']})"
            if eq.get("price_eur"):
                how = "in the package" if eq.get("price_status") == "package" else "as the option"
                text += f"; from {money(eq['price_eur'], 'EUR')} {how} '{eq['price_item']}'"
            text += "."
            row = eq["rows"][0] if eq.get("rows") else None
            url, at = self._src(row["source"]) if row else ("", None)
            self.add(f"{k}.eq.{item}", "equipment", text, st, node=f"cequip:{row['row_id']}" if row else node,
                     kind="web" if row else "derived", ref=url or "data/processed/competitor_equipment.csv", key=at,
                     feature=R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS[item]["feature"], series=s, market=m)
        for j, r in enumerate(c["ratings"], start=1):
            url, at = self._src(r["source"])
            n = f" from {int(r['n_reviews']):,} reviews" if r.get("n_reviews") else ""
            text = f"{r['publisher']} {r['kind'].replace('_', ' ')} for the {name}: {r['score']:g} of {r['scale_max']:g}{n}"
            if r.get("bmw"):
                b = r["bmw"]
                bn = f" from {int(b['n_reviews']):,} reviews" if b.get("n_reviews") else ""
                text += f"; the {bname} scores {b['score']:g} of {b['scale_max']:g}{bn} on the same publisher"
            self.add(f"{k}.rating{j}", "rating", text + ".", r["score"], node=f"crating:{r['row_id']}", ref=url, key=at,
                     series=s, market=m)
        self._reviews(k, t, c, name)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ summary
    def _summary(self, p, t):
        s, m, bmw = t["series"], t["market"], t["bmw"]
        sm = t["summary"]
        pr = sm.get("price")
        if pr:
            n, rank = pr["n_models"], pr["bmw_rank_from_cheapest"]
            d = pr["bmw_vs_median_abs"]
            rel = ("equal to" if d == 0 else f"{money(abs(d), pr['currency'])} ({abs(pr['bmw_vs_median_pct']):.1f}%) "
                   f"{'above' if d > 0 else 'below'}")
            self.add(f"{p}.price_rank", "summary", f"Of the {t['series_name']} and its {pr['n_competitors_priced']} "
                     f"competitors with a comparable price in {t['reference']['country_name']}, the {t['series_name']} "
                     f"has entry price rank {rank} of {n} (1 = cheapest); its entry price is {rel} the competitors' "
                     f"median of {money(pr['median_competitor'], pr['currency'])}.", rank, kind="derived",
                     node=f"series:{s}", ref="competitors/engine.py", series=s, market=m)
        for item, counts in sm.get("equipment", {}).items():
            label = R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS[item]["label"]
            n = sum(counts.values())
            parts = [f"{v} {STATUS_TEXT[k]}" for k, v in counts.items() if v]
            self.add(f"{p}.eq.{item}", "equipment", f"{label} across the {n} competitors of the {t['series_name']} in "
                     f"{t['market_name']} (German-market equipment): {'; '.join(parts)}.", counts.get("standard", 0),
                     kind="derived", node=f"series:{s}", ref="competitors/engine.py",
                     feature=R.EQUIPMENT_ITEMS[item]["feature"], series=s, market=m)


def build_bundle(comparison: dict, graph=None, cid: str = "") -> tuple[FactBundle, list[str]]:
    b = CompetitorFactBuilder(comparison, graph, cid)
    return b.build(), b.missing_nodes

"""Agents 4 + 5: competitor analysis and its presentation for the report's price & equipment section.

    CompetitionService.compare(series, markets, features)   CompetitorEngine -> facts (no LLM, instant)
    CompetitionService.analyse(competition_id)               Agent 4 analyst -> verifier -> one rewrite -> strip
                                                              Agent 5 presenter -> verifier -> analyst fallback

Agent 4 (OPENAI_ANALYST_MODEL) compares BMW with its top five competitors per series x market and writes findings,
each citing competitor fact IDs; it runs once per series (in parallel) on that series' facts. The verifier's rules
(citations, numbers, labels, quotes, series/market scope), two extra rules (the finding's series and market match
its facts; it cites a fact of its dimension) and the semantic judge check every finding. Failing findings go back
once and are removed if they still fail.

Agent 5 (OPENAI_PRESENTER_MODEL) turns the verified findings into a short plain-language brief. Its sentences are
verified the same way; a sentence that fails is replaced by the verified finding(s) it was based on, so nothing
unverified is shown and nothing verified is lost.
"""

import threading
import time
from collections import OrderedDict
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from .. import config
from ..competitors import registry as CR
from ..competitors.engine import CompetitorEngine
from ..competitors.facts import build_bundle, competition_id
from . import verifier
from .contracts import (BRIEF_SECTIONS, DIMENSION_GROUPS, Check, CompetitorAnalysisLLM, CompetitorBriefLLM, FactBundle,
                        Finding, PresentedClaim)
from .llm import LLMOutputInvalid, LLMUnavailable

MAX_CACHED = 64
NO_KEY = ("No OpenAI API key is configured, so the competitor analysis and presentation agents cannot run. The "
          "comparison tables come straight from the collected data and do not need the key.")
SERIES_NAMES = {"F70": "1 Series (F70)", "G60": "5 Series (G60)", "G70": "7 Series (G70)"}

ANALYST_INSTRUCTIONS = """You are the competitor analysis agent of BMW's product-idea evaluator. Your reader is a BMW product manager who is evaluating an idea for the 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60) or 7 Series (G70) and wants to know how BMW stands against its competitors.

You receive FACTS, one per line as "ID | statement", computed from public web data (sales, list prices, technical data, German-market equipment, ratings and classified review statements) and from BMW's own German price list. For each series and market they name the top five competitors and compare them with BMW. They are your only source of truth.

Write findings that compare BMW with its competitors. For every series and market that has a competitor set in the facts, write 3 to 7 findings, choosing the dimensions that matter most for the IDEA:
- selection: who the main rivals are and why (sales);
- price: where BMW's entry price sits against the rivals (rank, gaps, powertrain prices);
- equipment: how the rivals offer the equipment the idea is about, against BMW (German market);
- product: notable differences in power, size, boot or electric range;
- sales: BMW's volume against the rivals in the same source;
- customers: ratings from the same publisher and the topics reviewers praise or criticise.
Each finding is one sentence with its series, market and dimension.

Rules - a verifier checks every finding and deletes those that break them:
1. fact_ids lists every fact whose number, name, label, quote, series or market the finding uses. Cite at least one fact of the finding's series and market, and one of its dimension.
2. Use only numbers written in the cited facts, at the same or fewer decimals. Never add, subtract, average, convert or count yourself; the facts already state gaps, percentages and ranks.
3. Make the direction explicit: say which car is cheaper, more powerful, sells more, or offers the equipment as standard.
4. Put words in double quotes only when copied exactly from a cited quote fact.
5. Name a series or market only when a cited fact is about it. Write '1 Series (F70)', '5 Series (G60)', '7 Series (G70)', 'Europe', 'United States', 'China', 'Rest of world'. Name competitors as the facts do.
6. No causes, forecasts or general knowledge the facts do not state. Where data is missing or not comparable, say so plainly instead of guessing.
7. Short, direct sentences. No filler, no marketing language."""

PRESENTER_INSTRUCTIONS = """You are the presentation agent of BMW's product-idea evaluator. You turn the competitor analyst's verified FINDINGS into a short, plain-language brief that sits next to the price and equipment section of a report for a busy BMW product manager.

You receive the IDEA, the verified FINDINGS ("ID | series | market | dimension | text | cited facts") and the FACTS they cite ("ID | statement").

Write:
- headline: one sentence on how BMW stands against its competitors for this idea.
- price_position: 1-3 sentences on BMW's price against the rivals.
- equipment: 1-3 sentences on how the rivals offer the equipment the idea is about, against BMW (say when the facts have no equipment data for it).
- product_and_sales: 0-3 sentences on product and sales differences that matter for the idea.
- customer_view: 0-2 sentences on what ratings and reviewers say about the rivals.
- implications: 1-3 sentences on what the comparison means for the idea - only what the findings support; phrase them as points to weigh, not forecasts.
- caveats: 1-2 sentences on the limits of this comparison.

Rules - a verifier checks every sentence; one that fails is replaced by the analyst's original finding:
1. Restate the findings in plain words; do not add facts. For each sentence list in finding_ids the findings it restates or combines, and in fact_ids every fact whose number, name, label, quote, series or market it uses.
2. Use only numbers written in the cited facts, at the same or fewer decimals. Never compute.
3. Name a series or market only when a cited fact is about it ('1 Series (F70)', '5 Series (G60)', '7 Series (G70)', 'Europe', 'United States', 'China', 'Rest of world').
4. Double quotes only for words copied exactly from a cited quote fact.
5. Plain words: no jargon, no marketing language, one idea per sentence."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def _lines(facts) -> str:
    return "\n".join(f"{f.id} | {f.statement}" for f in facts)


def _facts_for(bundle: FactBundle, series: str) -> list:
    """The facts of one series plus the shared ones (data version, caveats, features without equipment data)."""
    return [f for f in bundle.facts if f.series == series or f.series is None]


def _scope_text(scope: dict) -> str:
    feats = ", ".join(scope.get("features") or []) or "none (no matching feature)"
    return (f"IDEA: {scope.get('idea') or '(not given)'}\nSCOPE: features {feats}; series "
            f"{', '.join(scope.get('series') or []) or 'all'}; markets {', '.join(scope.get('markets') or []) or 'all'}; "
            f"move {scope.get('move') or 'unspecified'}.")


def finding_rules(meta: dict):
    """Extra rules for analyst findings: series/market and dimension must match the cited facts."""
    def run(claim, index) -> list[Check]:
        m = meta.get(claim.id) or {}
        cited = [index[i] for i in claim.fact_ids if i in index]
        tuple_ok = any(f.series == m.get("series") and f.market == m.get("market") for f in cited)
        groups = DIMENSION_GROUPS.get(m.get("dimension"), set())
        dim_ok = any(f.group in groups for f in cited)
        return [Check(name="tuple", passed=tuple_ok,
                      detail=(f"Cites a fact of {m.get('series')} {m.get('market')}." if tuple_ok else
                              f"No cited fact is about {m.get('series')} in {m.get('market')}.")),
                Check(name="dimension", passed=dim_ok,
                      detail=(f"Cites a {m.get('dimension')} fact." if dim_ok else
                              f"No cited fact is of the '{m.get('dimension')}' kind ({', '.join(sorted(groups))})."))]
    return run


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Agent 4
def analyse_series(llm, bundle: FactBundle, scope: dict, series: str, start: int) -> dict:
    """Analyst for one series: draft, verify, one rewrite of what failed, verify again."""
    facts = _facts_for(bundle, series)
    sub = FactBundle(evaluation_id=bundle.evaluation_id, idea=bundle.idea, facts=facts)
    base = f"{_scope_text(scope)}\nSERIES OF THIS ANALYSIS: {SERIES_NAMES[series]}\n\nFACTS (ID | statement):\n{_lines(facts)}"

    def draft(prompt: str, attempt: int, offset: int) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict]:
        out = llm.parse("analyst", ANALYST_INSTRUCTIONS, prompt, CompetitorAnalysisLLM)
        claims, meta = [], {}
        for f in out.findings:
            if not f.text.strip():
                continue
            cid = f"a{offset + len(claims) + 1}"
            ids = list(dict.fromkeys(i.strip() for i in f.fact_ids if i.strip()))
            claims.append(Finding(id=cid, section=f.dimension, text=f.text.strip(), fact_ids=ids, attempt=attempt,
                                  series=f.series, market=f.market))
            meta[cid] = {"series": f.series, "market": f.market, "dimension": f.dimension}
        return claims, meta

    claims, meta = draft(base, 1, start)
    claims = verifier.verify(claims, sub, llm, extra=finding_rules(meta))
    rewritten, attempts = [], 1
    failed = [c for c in claims if c.status == "removed"]
    if failed:
        rewritten = failed
        lines = []
        for c in failed:
            why = "; ".join(f"{ch.name}: {ch.detail}" for ch in c.checks if not ch.passed)
            lines.append(f"- [{c.series} {c.market} {c.section}] \"{c.text}\" (cited {', '.join(c.fact_ids) or 'nothing'})"
                         f" -> {why}")
        prompt = (base + "\n\nYOUR PREVIOUS FINDINGS FAILED VERIFICATION FOR THESE. Write all findings again; fix each "
                  "of these so that it follows the rules, or drop it:\n" + "\n".join(lines))
        kept = [c for c in claims if c.status == "verified"]
        again, meta2 = draft(prompt, 2, start + len(claims))
        again = verifier.verify(again, sub, llm, extra=finding_rules(meta2))
        claims = again if any(c.status == "verified" for c in again) or not kept else again + kept
        attempts = 2
    return {"series": series, "claims": claims, "rewritten": rewritten, "attempts": attempts}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Agent 5
def present(llm, bundle: FactBundle, scope: dict, findings: list[Finding]) -> tuple[dict, list[PresentedClaim]]:
    index = bundle.index()
    cited = list(dict.fromkeys(i for f in findings for i in f.fact_ids))
    shared = [f.id for f in bundle.facts if f.group == "caveat"]
    facts = [index[i] for i in dict.fromkeys(cited + shared) if i in index]
    flines = "\n".join(f"{f.id} | {f.series} | {f.market} | {f.section} | {f.text} | {', '.join(f.fact_ids)}"
                       for f in findings)
    prompt = (f"{_scope_text(scope)}\n\nFINDINGS (ID | series | market | dimension | text | cited facts):\n{flines}"
              f"\n\nFACTS (ID | statement):\n{_lines(facts)}")
    draft = llm.parse("presenter", PRESENTER_INSTRUCTIONS, prompt, CompetitorBriefLLM)
    if not draft.headline.text.strip():
        raise LLMOutputInvalid("The presenter returned an empty headline.", ["headline.text: empty"])
    by_id = {f.id: f for f in findings}
    claims, n = [], 0
    for section in BRIEF_SECTIONS:
        items = [draft.headline] if section == "headline" else getattr(draft, section)
        for c in items:
            if not c.text.strip():
                continue
            n += 1
            claims.append(PresentedClaim(id=f"p{n}", section=section, text=c.text.strip(),
                                         fact_ids=list(dict.fromkeys(i.strip() for i in c.fact_ids if i.strip())),
                                         finding_ids=[i for i in dict.fromkeys(c.finding_ids) if i in by_id]))
    claims = verifier.verify(claims, bundle, llm)
    shown: dict[str, list] = {s: [] for s in BRIEF_SECTIONS}
    used_findings: set = set()
    for c in claims:
        if c.status == "verified":
            shown[c.section].append(c)
            used_findings |= set(c.finding_ids)
    for c in claims:                                   # fall back to the verified findings behind a failed sentence
        if c.status != "removed":
            continue
        for fid in c.finding_ids:
            if fid in used_findings:
                continue
            f = by_id[fid]
            used_findings.add(fid)
            shown[c.section].append(PresentedClaim(id=f"{c.id}-{fid}", section=c.section, text=f.text,
                                                   fact_ids=f.fact_ids, finding_ids=[fid], origin="analyst_fallback",
                                                   checks=f.checks, attempt=f.attempt))
    return shown, claims


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- service
class CompetitionService:
    def __init__(self, graph=None, llm_getter=None, ctx=None, parallel: bool = True):
        self.engine = CompetitorEngine()
        self.g = graph
        self.llm_getter = llm_getter or (lambda: None)
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.parallel = parallel
        self._cache: OrderedDict = OrderedDict()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def status(self) -> dict:
        return self.engine.status()

    def compare(self, series=None, markets=None, features=None, idea: str = "", move: str = "") -> dict:
        series = [s for s in (series or []) if s in config.MODELS]
        markets = [m for m in (markets or []) if m in CR.MARKETS]
        features = list(dict.fromkeys(features or []))
        domains = {}
        if self.ctx is not None:
            domains = {f: str(self.ctx.features.loc[f, "domain"]) for f in features if f in self.ctx.features.index}
        comparison = self.engine.compare(series or None, markets or None, features, domains)
        if not comparison.get("available"):
            return {"competition_id": None, "available": False, "comparison": comparison, "facts": []}
        scope = {"series": series, "markets": markets, "features": features, "idea": idea, "move": move}
        cid = competition_id({k: scope[k] for k in ("series", "markets", "features")}, comparison["data_hash"])
        bundle, missing = build_bundle(comparison, self.g, cid)
        with self._lock:
            prev = self._cache.get(cid)
            self._cache[cid] = {"scope": scope, "comparison": comparison, "bundle": bundle,
                                "analysed": prev["analysed"] if prev else None}
            self._cache.move_to_end(cid)
            while len(self._cache) > MAX_CACHED:
                self._cache.popitem(last=False)
        return {"competition_id": cid, "available": True, "comparison": comparison,
                "facts": [f.model_dump() for f in bundle.facts], "graph_missing_nodes": len(missing)}

    def analyse(self, cid: str, force: bool = False) -> dict:
        with self._lock:
            entry = self._cache.get(cid)
        if entry is None:
            raise KeyError(cid)
        if entry["analysed"] and not force:
            return entry["analysed"]
        llm = self.llm_getter()
        if llm is None:
            raise LLMUnavailable(NO_KEY)
        t0 = time.time()
        bundle, scope = entry["bundle"], entry["scope"]
        series = [t["series"] for t in entry["comparison"]["tuples"] if t["status"] == "ok"]
        series = list(dict.fromkeys(series))
        if not series:
            out = {"competition_id": cid, "analysis": {"findings": [], "removed": [], "rewritten": [], "attempts": 0,
                                                       "model": llm.models.get("analyst")},
                   "brief": None, "verification": None, "seconds": 0.0,
                   "message": "No series in scope has a competitor set, so there is nothing to analyse."}
            entry["analysed"] = out
            return out
        offsets = {s: i * 100 for i, s in enumerate(series)}
        if self.parallel and len(series) > 1:
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(series)) as ex:
                results = list(ex.map(lambda s: analyse_series(llm, bundle, scope, s, offsets[s]), series))
        else:
            results = [analyse_series(llm, bundle, scope, s, offsets[s]) for s in series]
        claims = [c for r in results for c in r["claims"]]
        findings = [c for c in claims if c.status == "verified"]
        analysis = {"model": llm.models.get("analyst"), "attempts": max(r["attempts"] for r in results),
                    "findings": [c.model_dump() for c in findings],
                    "removed": [c.model_dump() for c in claims if c.status == "removed"],
                    "rewritten": [c.model_dump() for r in results for c in r["rewritten"]]}
        brief, verification = None, None
        if findings:
            shown, pclaims = present(llm, bundle, scope, findings)
            brief = {"model": llm.models.get("presenter"),
                     "sections": {s: [c.model_dump() for c in v] for s, v in shown.items()}}
            verification = {"rules": verifier.RULES + ["tuple", "dimension"], "semantic_model": llm.models.get("verifier"),
                            "presented": [c.model_dump() for c in pclaims],
                            "n_presented_verified": sum(c.status == "verified" for c in pclaims),
                            "n_presented_replaced": sum(c.status == "removed" for c in pclaims),
                            "n_findings_verified": len(findings),
                            "n_findings_removed": len(analysis["removed"])}
        out = {"competition_id": cid, "analysis": analysis, "brief": brief, "verification": verification,
               "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
               "message": None if findings else "No finding passed verification, so there is no written comparison."}
        entry["analysed"] = out
        return out

Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.296/a2498a5de4dde9df3f54af0c9e3514f3/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

"""Competitor data, comparison and the two competitor agents. No network: a scripted fake stands in for OpenAI.

The synthetic tests build from rows written to a temporary folder; the data tests check the processed tables
written by `python -m bmw_feedback competitors build` and are skipped when those are absent.
"""

import json
import re

import pandas as pd
import pytest

from bmw_feedback import config
from bmw_feedback.agents import competition, verifier
from bmw_feedback.agents.contracts import (CompetitorAnalysisLLM, CompetitorBriefLLM, FactBundle, FindingLLM,
                                           PresentedClaimLLM)
from bmw_feedback.competitors import build, records, registry, snapshot
from conftest import FakeLLM, judge_all

HAS_TABLES = build.load_tables() is not None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- validator
@pytest.mark.parametrize("text,value,ok", [
    ("2025 fell 23.1 percent to 13,575", 13575, True), ("Preis 62.300,00 €", 62300, True), ("ab 1.190 Euro", 1190, True),
    ("指导价43.99万元", 439900, True), ("$58,450 MSRP", 58450, True), ("6,1 s", 6.1, True), ("5 060 mm", 5060, True),
    ("13,575", 13576, False), ("1.190 Euro", 119, False), ("E200", 200, False),
])
def test_numbers_in_evidence(text, value, ok):
    assert records.number_in(value, text) is ok


@pytest.fixture
def sandbox(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Snapshot, text and extracted folders in a temporary directory, with one saved page."""
    raw, txt, ext = tmp_path / "raw", tmp_path / "text", tmp_path / "extracted"
    for d in (raw, txt, ext):
        d.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.setattr(snapshot, "RAW_DIR", raw)
    monkeypatch.setattr(snapshot, "TEXT_DIR", txt)
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "EXTRACTED_DIR", ext)

    def page(sid, text, publisher="example.org"):
        (raw / sid).mkdir()
        (raw / sid / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "source_id": sid, "url": f"https://{publisher}/{sid}", "final_url": f"https://{publisher}/{sid}",
            "publisher": publisher, "title": sid, "retrieved_at": "2026-10-11T10:00:00+0200", "kind": "html",
            "rendered": False, "sha256": "0" * 64, "bytes": len(text), "ok": True}))
        (txt / f"{sid}.txt").write_text(text)

    def rows(name, items):
        (ext / name).write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in items) + "\n")

    return page, rows, ext


def test_validator_rejects_invented_values(sandbox):
    page, _, _ = sandbox
    page("s0000000001", "In 2025 the E-Class sold 13,575 units in the US.\nBase MSRP $63,050 for the E 350.")
    base = {"table": "sales", "model_id": "mercedes-e-class", "market": "US", "region": "United States", "year": 2025,
            "units": 13575, "basis": "sales", "tier": "aggregator", "source_id": "s0000000001",
            "evidence": "In 2025 the E-Class sold 13,575 units"}
    assert records.validate_record(base) == []
    assert any("not written in the evidence" in e for e in records.validate_record({**base, "units": 13600}))
    assert any("not in source" in e for e in records.validate_record({**base, "evidence": "sold 14,000 units"}))
    assert any("unknown source_id" in e for e in records.validate_record({**base, "source_id": "s9999999999"}))
    assert any("basis must be" in e for e in records.validate_record({**base, "basis": "guess"}))
    price = {"table": "price", "model_id": "bmw-5-series", "market": "EU", "country": "DE", "currency": "EUR",
             "variant": "520i", "amount": 63050, "powertrain": "ICE", "price_type": "list_price", "tax_basis": "x",
             "source_id": "s0000000001", "evidence": "Base MSRP $63,050"}
    assert any("BMW's own DE price list" in e for e in records.validate_record(price))
    wrong_cur = {**price, "model_id": "mercedes-e-class", "currency": "USD"}
    assert any("must be in EUR" in e for e in records.validate_record(wrong_cur))


def test_selection_ranks_by_segment_sales_and_falls_back_to_rivals(sandbox, monkeypatch):
    page, rows, ext = sandbox
    lines = [f"Model {i} sold {u:,} units in 2025 in Europe." for i, u in enumerate([9000, 7000, 5000, 3000], start=1)]
    page("s0000000001", "\n".join(lines) + "\nThe BMW sold 8,000 units in 2025 in Europe.")
    page("s0000000002", "Rivals: the Rival Five and the Rival Six are named as 5 Series competitors.", "press.example")
    models = [{"table": "model", "model_id": f"maker-m{i}", "brand": "Maker", "model": f"M{i}", "segment": "executive",
               "body": "saloon"} for i in range(1, 7)]
    models.append({"table": "model", "model_id": "bmw-5-series", "brand": "BMW", "model": "5 Series",
                   "segment": "executive", "body": "saloon"})
    models.append({"table": "model", "model_id": "maker-compact", "brand": "Maker", "model": "C", "segment": "compact",
                   "body": "hatch"})
    sales = [{"table": "sales", "model_id": f"maker-m{i}", "market": "EU", "region": "Europe (EU+EFTA+UK)",
              "year": 2025, "units": u, "basis": "registrations", "tier": "aggregator", "source_id": "s0000000001",
              "evidence": f"Model {i} sold {u:,} units in 2025 in Europe."}
             for i, u in enumerate([9000, 7000, 5000, 3000], start=1)]
    sales.append({"table": "sales", "model_id": "bmw-5-series", "market": "EU", "region": "Europe (EU+EFTA+UK)",
                  "year": 2025, "units": 8000, "basis": "registrations", "tier": "aggregator",
                  "source_id": "s0000000001", "evidence": "The BMW sold 8,000 units in 2025 in Europe."})
    rivals = [{"table": "rival", "model_id": mid, "bmw_series": "G60", "market": "EU", "source_id": "s0000000002",
               "evidence": "Rivals: the Rival Five and the Rival Six are named as 5 Series competitors."}
              for mid in ("maker-m5", "maker-m6", "maker-compact")]
    # a rival counts only if it is present in the market (a price or sales row there)
    prices = [{"table": "price", "model_id": mid, "market": "EU", "country": "DE", "currency": "EUR",
               "variant": "Base", "amount": 50000 + i, "powertrain": "ICE", "price_type": "list_price",
               "tax_basis": "incl. 19% VAT", "entry": True, "source_id": "s0000000003",
               "evidence": f"Base {50000 + i:,} EUR"} for i, mid in enumerate(["maker-m5", "maker-compact"])]
    page("s0000000003", "Base 50,000 EUR. Base 50,001 EUR.")
    rows("all.jsonl", models + sales + rivals + prices)
    tables, quality = build.build()
    sets = tables["sets"]
    g = sets[(sets["series"] == "G60") & (sets["market"] == "EU")].sort_values("rank")
    assert list(g["model_id"]) == ["maker-m1", "maker-m2", "maker-m3", "maker-m4", "maker-m5"]
    assert list(g["basis"]) == ["sales"] * 4 + ["rival_mentions"]
    assert "bmw-5-series" not in set(g["model_id"])                       # BMW is never its own competitor
    f70 = sets[(sets["series"] == "F70") & (sets["market"] == "US")]
    assert f70["basis"].tolist() == ["not_sold"]                         # sales_volumes.xlsx: no F70 in the US

def test_analyst_rewrites_then_presenter_falls_back_to_verified_findings():
    good = FindingLLM(series="G60", market="EU", dimension="price", fact_ids=["cx.G60.EU.c1.entry"],
                      text="In Europe the Mercedes-Benz E-Class starts EUR 2,000 (3.3%) above the 5 Series (G60).")
    bad = FindingLLM(series="G60", market="EU", dimension="price", fact_ids=["cx.G60.EU.c1.entry"],
                     text="In Europe the E-Class costs EUR 2,500 more than the 5 Series (G60).")
    fixed = FindingLLM(series="G60", market="EU", dimension="selection", fact_ids=["cx.G60.EU.set"],
                       text="In Europe the Mercedes-Benz E-Class is the best-selling rival of the 5 Series (G60), "
                            "with 61,000 units.")
    llm = FakeLLM({
        "analyst": [CompetitorAnalysisLLM(findings=[good, bad]), CompetitorAnalysisLLM(findings=[good, fixed])],
        "verifier": [judge_all(), judge_all(), judge_all(unsupported_text="cheaper")],
        "presenter": [CompetitorBriefLLM(
            headline=PresentedClaimLLM(text="In Europe the 5 Series (G60) starts below the E-Class.",
                                       fact_ids=["cx.G60.EU.c1.entry"], finding_ids=["a3"]),
            price_position=[PresentedClaimLLM(text="The E-Class is cheaper than the 5 Series (G60) in Europe.",
                                              fact_ids=["cx.G60.EU.c1.entry"], finding_ids=["a3"])],
            equipment=[], product_and_sales=[], customer_view=[], implications=[],
            caveats=[PresentedClaimLLM(text="Prices are list prices without discounts.",
                                       fact_ids=["cx.caveat.list-prices"], finding_ids=[])])],
    })
    res = competition.analyse_series(llm, _bundle(), {"features": [], "idea": "x"}, "G60", 0)
    assert res["attempts"] == 2 and [c.text for c in res["rewritten"]] == [bad.text]
    verified = [c for c in res["claims"] if c.status == "verified"]
    assert {c.section for c in verified} == {"price", "selection"}
    shown, claims = competition.present(llm, _bundle(), {"features": [], "idea": "x"}, verified)
    status = {c.text: c.status for c in claims}
    assert status["The E-Class is cheaper than the 5 Series (G60) in Europe."] == "removed"     # judged unsupported
    assert [c.origin for c in shown["price_position"]] == ["analyst_fallback"]                 # replaced by finding a3
    assert shown["price_position"][0].text == verified[0].text
    assert shown["headline"] and shown["caveats"]
